title: Faceted Flight 2 edition preset
description:
One presentation preset, as data. `classic` is the ledger as it stands — every flag off, every number the shipped one. `anniversary` is a curated set of further deviations, each one a DEV row, each individually switchable here. docs/plan/ANNIVERSARY.md section 0 is the argument.

THE PRESET IS CONTENT, NOT CODE (hard rule 6, rule 3): the tuning numbers for an Anniversary feature live in the preset JSON, and `src/` reads them. A number typed into `src/render/` would be indistinguishable from an extracted one in six months.

THIS SCHEMA IS A GATE: `additionalProperties` is false at every level, so a feature that grows a tuning key has to declare it here, in `src/content/edition-schema.ts`, and in BOTH preset files — `tests/unit/edition-content.test.ts` refuses anything else.

curve.description: A tuning curve as `[x, y]` points in ASCENDING x — linear between them, FLAT outside them (never extrapolated: a ship at 500 m/s gets the 340 m/s value rather than a gain of 1.6). Two points minimum, because one is a constant written as a curve and zero is a hole. `validateEdition` re-checks the ordering at load, because `sampleCurve` walks the points once and assumes it.

linearRgb.description: LINEAR rgb, not sRGB — the same convention as `fx.motes.colorLight`. A light's colour and an emissive floor are radiance, and putting a swatch picked in an sRGB picker here makes them darker and more saturated than the number reads.

rampStop.description: One stop of a light-RESPONSE ramp, LINEAR rgb, capped at 1. Not `linearRgb`, and the cap is the difference: a stop is the multiplier a light's own radiance is scaled by, so a value above 1 is an overbright and belongs in the ramp's own `overbright` gain where one number moves the whole curve. The POSITIONS of the stops are not authored anywhere — see `render.illustrative`.

metres3.description: [x, y, z] in METRES from the EYE, in the ship's frame as three sees it: −z is forward and +y is up, the convention `game/flight.ts`'s `EYE` and `ART_POSITION` are written in. Relative to the eye rather than to the ship origin because these are placements inside a cabin around a head.

intensity.description: three `PointLight.intensity`, candela with `decay: 2`. Never negative: three will happily subtract light, and a lamp that darkens the cabin gets diagnosed as a shader bug. `validateEdition` refuses it too.

distance.description: Metres. Past this the light contributes nothing, which is the ONLY thing confining it to the cockpit — three has no per-object light mask, and a layer would turn the light off rather than scope it (DEV-043, and `render/cockpit-interior.ts`'s header cites the line in three that does it).

decay.description: 2 is the physically correct inverse square, and is what the rest of the game's lighting assumes.

cockpitLight.description: One point light in the cabin. Each one is a `NUM_POINT_LIGHTS` change, so it recompiles every lit material's program ONCE — at boot on this preset, and again on a flip. ANNIVERSARY.md V8, DEV-088.

palette.description: Colours an instance picks from, uniformly. Empty is legal and means the band draws nothing — which is what Classic's empty lists are.

lifeLeapers.description: Animals that leap from the sea (DEV-449), one kind a block, one draw a kind: polyfish's own models (Matt's; `tools/assets/convert-life.mjs` bakes the rigs' rest pose), placed in pods by RULE (`sim/life/pods.ts`: aimed at the course's line and spawn as the boats are, in water at least `depth` deep, open ocean included), each leaping a ballistic arc once a period — a pure function of the clock — from and into the water the shader drew. Under the water they are not drawn. Never a collider, never a score.

minQuality.description: The lowest comfort quality that still draws the kind.

mesh.description: The converted GLB under the asset base, `assets/life/…`.

gravity.description: M/S² the leap falls at. SCENERY's gravity, not the sim's 32: 2016 tuned the SHIPS against −32, and an animal thrown under it hangs two thirds as long as a real one.

alongRoute.description: Pods aimed at `(i + 0.5) / n` of the course's line.

routeReach.description: METRES out from each line point searched, `[min, max]`.

startReach.description: METRES out from the spawn searched, `[min, max]`.

depth.description: METRES of water a pod needs under it; open ocean counts.

podRadius.description: METRES a pod spreads round its centre.

swing.description: DEGREES either side of a pod's shared heading: a pod travels together.

period.description: SECONDS between one animal's leaps, `[min, max]`. THE NUMBER TO ARGUE WITH for how lively the sea is.

height.description: METRES a leap clears the water by.

length.description: METRES a leap covers, entry to entry.

scale.description: Uniform scale on the mesh: polyfish's units are not metres (its dolphin is 0.1725 long).

lineAbove.description: DEV-532: METRES the course's line may stand over the sea's base at an `alongRoute` aim and still aim a pod there. Absent: every aim. A pod under a line flown hundreds of metres up is one nobody sees; this puts the aims where the lap comes down to the water.

breach.description: DEV-532: the pod leaps TOGETHER as the player comes at it (`sim/life/pods.ts` `breachDue`), every animal once, `stagger` seconds apart, cued so the arcs' apex falls `apexAhead` metres ahead at the closing speed; then it rests and goes back to its period. Absent: the period alone (DEV-449). Scenery that reacts to the eye, never a gameplay rule.

apexAhead.description: METRES ahead of the eye the apex falls. THE NUMBER TO ARGUE WITH for how close the breach is.

below.description: DEGREES under the eye's level the apex may fall, at most: from a height h the apex is kept h / tan(below) out, so a high eye still has it in the frame (the cockpit reaches 35 degrees down).

ahead.description: DEGREES either side of the eye's travel the pod must stand in to be cued.

reach.description: METRES: the farthest a pod is cued from.

minSpeed.description: M/S the eye must be making: a player standing on the deck cues nothing.

stagger.description: SECONDS between one animal of the pod leaving the water and the next.

rest.description: SECONDS a pod rests after a breach before it can be cued again.

id.description: Matches the file's basename. `boot/settings.ts` stores this id; `?edition=<id>` overrides it for one load.

note.description: One line for a person reading the file.

toneMapping.description: three.js tone mapping on the one renderer. `none` is what shipped: linear to sRGB, clamped, which is what Unity 5 did in a Linear project and is the reason a 4-degree sun and an additive streak land on the same flat 1.0. ANNIVERSARY.md V1, DEV-081.

exposure.description: `renderer.toneMappingExposure`. 1 is unity. Pushed as a uniform on every draw, so it costs no recompile and a lookdev slider moves it live. Only meaningful with a tone mapper — `none` reads it and multiplies nothing by it. V1, DEV-081.

startDistance.description: Metres. Nothing nearer than this is touched at all — the near field is the one thing the mission fog already handles well and the one thing a haze term must not muddy.

range.description: Metres from `startDistance` to full strength. The shader is handed 1/range, so this may not be zero.

strength.description: How far toward `tint` at full range. 0 is no shift at any distance.

desaturate.description: How far toward the surface colour's own Rec.709 luminance at full range. 0 is no desaturation at any distance.

tint.description: sRGB 0..1, the way `fog.color` in a level is. Linearised in `render/unity-fog.ts` by the same function that linearises the fog colour, because both are mixed against a linear framebuffer.

haze.description: Aerial perspective as its own term — a distance-driven desaturation and cool shift of the surface's OWN colour, opacity-free, applied before the fog mixes the sky over it. Leaves the near field alone. NOT the mission fog, which stays faithful (DEV-018/018b). ANNIVERSARY.md V4, DEV-082.

shadow.description: The response at Half-Lambert 0 — a facet turned fully away from the sun. Cool, and deliberately not black: this is the term that lifts a shadow-side facet off the ambient-only floor. It is multiplied by the sun's OWN colour, which on `int_01` is a warm (0.831, 0.569, 0.391) at intensity 1.3 — so a cool stop against a warm sun produces a near-neutral fill rather than a blue one, which is the honest physics of a response curve and is recorded in DEV-092.

terminator.description: The response at Half-Lambert 0.5, which is `N·L = 0` EXACTLY: the terminator. Warm, and on a faceted world this is not a soft band — a facet edge-on to the 4-degree sun lands here and takes this colour whole. Stock Lambert gives 0 at this point, so whatever is here is entirely new light.

lit.description: The response at Half-Lambert 1 — a facet square to the sun. Keep it near 1 or the whole world's key light changes brightness rather than colour, which is a job for `render.exposure`.

overbright.description: A flat gain over the whole ramp — the TF2 paper's post-lookup `×N`, which is why it is separate from the stops rather than baked into `lit`: it keeps the three stops inside 0..1 where a ramp belongs, and it is the one number that moves the key light's LEVEL without touching its shape. 1 is no gain.

strength.description: The cross-fade from the stock `saturate(N·L)` response to the ramp. 0 is the EXACT identity, not nearly: GLSL's `mix(x, y, 0.0)` is `x * 1.0 + y * 0.0`, which is `x` for any finite `y`, and the ramp is bounded. That identity is what lets both presets compile one program (`render/program-cache-key.ts`) and is asserted with exact floats in `tests/unit/illustrative.test.ts`. Ship the ramp at the strength you mean and leave this at 1, so it stays a clean A/B dial rather than a second tuning number.

illustrative.description: The illustrative diffuse warp from "Illustrative Rendering in Team Fortress 2" (Mitchell/Francke/Eng, NPAR 2007): replace the direct diffuse response `saturate(N·L)` with a ramp indexed by Half-Lambert `N·L * 0.5 + 0.5`, so the cool/warm shift sits INSIDE the shadow term instead of over the whole frame. Applied to the LAND terrains (the Marmoset-authored materials) and to the generated props, never to the ocean, the specular, the ambient or the IBL. ANNIVERSARY.md V7, DEV-092.

mapSize.description: Shadow map edge in TEXELS, a power of two (`validateEdition` refuses anything else). With `boxHalfSize` it fixes the texel size — `2 * boxHalfSize / mapSize` — which is the number the shadow's edge quality and its acne are both governed by. 2048 against a 900 m box is 0.88 m a texel, against an 8 m terrain facet.

boxHalfSize.description: Half the follow box, in METRES: the shadow covers a sphere this wide around the CAMERA and nothing outside it. 2016's `ShadowManager.shadowDistance` was 384 m (research 04 section 9.2) and the port's is larger because one map with no cascades has to carry both the near ground and the ridge that shadows it. It also sets how high you can fly and still see the ground shadowed: at 700 m the ground 700 m below is at the edge of the box.

castDistance.description: METRES up-sun of the box that casters are gathered from — how far back the near plane is pushed. At a 4-degree sun a 1,536 m band of relief occupies 22 km along the ray (`casterSpan` in `src/render/shadows.ts` is that arithmetic), so the geometrically complete answer is most of the map; this is where we stop. On Simonet 3,500 m is most of the island. It is the one number that trades frame time for a shadow that is really there: every LOD-0 chunk inside the prism is drawn into the depth map.

bias.description: METRES of depth bias, pulling the receiver toward the light before the compare. NOT three's `shadow.bias`, which is in normalised depth and therefore silently means a different distance whenever `boxHalfSize` or `castDistance` move; `shadowBiasFor` converts. At a 4-degree sun a metre of depth bias shifts a shadow about 14 m down-sun (`1 / sin(4 deg)`), so this buys acne cover at a known price in peter-panning.

normalBias.description: METRES the lookup is moved along the receiver's own normal, which IS three's unit (`shadowmap_vertex` offsets the world position). It is the better tool for a grazing sun — on flat ground under a 4-degree light it moves the sample about 14 m through the depth gradient for every metre of offset — and it is expensive for the same reason: the leverage that kills the acne is the leverage that detaches the edge.

radius.description: PCF disk radius in shadow TEXELS. three 0.185.1's `PCFShadowMap` is a five-tap Vogel disk on a hardware `sampler2DShadow`, rotated per pixel by an interleaved gradient noise, and this scales it — so it is a real penumbra, roughly `radius * texelSize` metres wide. (`PCFSoftShadowMap` is DEPRECATED in this revision: `WebGLShadowMap.render` warns and substitutes `PCFShadowMap`.)

edgeFade.description: METRES inside the box's edge over which the map hands its verdict to the far-field terms (DEV-453). Across the band the map's shadow fades to lit and the canopy bake takes the direct sun back (`render/far-shadow.ts`'s `ff2ShadowCover`), so the edge of the map is a gradient and not a line. Matt, on alpine: "the 'far shadow' line is very noticable and jarring ... from it to the player, shadows exist, beyond it - no shadows". Zero is 2016's hard edge, which Matt called "an artifact i couldn't fix at the time", so neither preset ships it. Must be below `boxHalfSize` (`validateEdition` refuses otherwise). Measured in the box's own axes: across the sun it is metres on the ground; along it, metres of depth.

shadows.description: One directional shadow map from the mission sun, on an orthographic box that follows the camera and is snapped to whole texels so the edges do not swim. Casters are LOD-0 land chunks (2016: `shadowCastingMode = Off` above LOD 0), the hand-placed landmarks, the ship's exterior hull, and the SCATTER only while `props.scatterShadows.enabled` says so (DEV-224 — since DEV-304 that is true on Anniversary in flat and false in a headset, via `vr.disable`); receivers are land chunks at every LOD and every prop, the scatter included. 2016 had soft shadows out to 384 m and FF2 has had none. ANNIVERSARY.md V3, DEV-086. OFF at quality `low`, whatever this says, and UNMEASURED in a headset.

shipShadow.description: Keep the ship's EXTERIOR hull in the scene while the player is in the COCKPIT, so that it casts (DEV-305, wishlist #29). 2016 deactivates `Art/ThirdPerson` when you go inside and the port copied it, so the one shadow whose length a player can read against their own altitude -- their own ship's -- was never on the ground. Three cannot do this cheaply and the refusals are each a different line of `WebGLShadowMap`: `object.visible`, `material.visible` and the layer test (against the VIEW camera) are all read by the shadow pass as well as by the frame. So with this true the hull is DRAWN with `colorWrite` and `depthWrite` both off -- one draw call and the vertex work, nothing in the colour or the depth buffer, and the shadow pass unaffected because it renders three's own `_depthMaterial`. A real cost, which is why it is a flag. INERT while `render.shadows.enabled` is false or at quality `low`: `boot/app.ts` composes it with `shadowsEnabled`, so Classic draws no extra hull and writes no material flag. A DEVIATION from 2016. SEPARATE from the bug it sits on: the hull cast nothing in ANY view, because the flag was written on the glTF scene root and three reads `castShadow` on the Mesh -- `shadowMeshesOf` fixes that for both presets and is not this switch. READ IT WITH `render.cockpitShadow`: the hull surrounds the cockpit, so both on puts the airframe's own shadow across the dashboard.

missionShadows.description: The mission sun's shadow map in a MISSION, and the passes that ride on it: the cockpit's own map (`render.cockpitSelfShadow`), the near cascade (`render.nearShadow`), the hull drawn for its shadow (`render.shipShadow`) and the cockpit receiving (`render.cockpitShadow`). DEV-932. `render.shadows` stays the machinery for every scene: the hangar's 2016 key light (DEV-440) and the title's sun cast under it alone, so a preset's `vr.disable` can name this key to take the map out of a mission in a headset while the menus keep theirs. With it off the far-field term (`render.sunHeight`) still shadows the terrain at every distance, through `render/far-shadow.ts`'s no-map branch. INERT while `render.shadows` is off or at quality `low`.

cockpitShadow.description: Let the COCKPIT SHELL receive the shadow map (DEV-306, wishlist #30). `ShadowRole`'s `ship-cockpit` is documented "Neither" and that is a TRANSCRIPTION of 2016 rather than a decision -- `render/shadows.ts` argues against the cockpit CASTING (the canopy's own shadow across the dashboard at a 0.88 m texel and an 0.08 m near plane, which is shimmer you cannot look away from in a headset) and says nothing about receiving, which is a per-fragment sample on geometry already in the frame. True makes the cabin go dark when you fly into a ridge's shadow inside `render.shadows.boxHalfSize`; the far field is already there via `render.sunHeight` (DEV-116) and the two compose by the min the shader takes. This flag can never turn CASTING on -- `shadowFlagsFor`'s `ship-cockpit` row hard-codes `cast: false` and only the receive half is a preset's. INERT while `render.shadows.enabled` is false or at quality `low`, because `shadowReceiversFor` composes `shadowsEnabled`. A DEVIATION from 2016. READ IT WITH `render.shipShadow`.

mapSize.description: Near-map edge in TEXELS, a power of two (`validateEdition` refuses anything else). The box is not a number here: it is the cockpit shell's own bounding sphere, measured off the mesh every frame, so the texel is `2 * radius / mapSize` -- 3.3 mm at 2048 against the shell's 3.38 m sphere (the shell is the whole airframe, wings and tail included; `tests/unit/cockpit-self-shadow.test.ts` measures it off the GLB).

bias.description: METRES of depth bias, pulling the receiver toward the light before the compare -- `render.shadows.bias`'s unit and its reason: three's own number is normalised depth and would mean a different distance whenever the box moves. Converted against the near box's depth (`2 * radius`) every frame, and SCALED BY SLOPE in the shader: `bias * (1 + min(tan(angle to the sun), 4))`, because a facet the sun grazes has a depth that changes fast across the filter's footprint and that is where flat-shaded acne lives (DEV-323 photographed 4 mm and 1 cm hatching the nose and the canopy struts; 2-3 cm with the slope term was clean at a 38-degree and a 4-degree sun).

normalBias.description: METRES the lookup is moved along the receiver's own normal, in the vertex shader, as three's own `shadowmap_vertex` does for the sun's map. The acne knob for a surface grazing the sun.

radius.description: Tap spacing of the PCF square, in near-map TEXELS: nine hardware-compared taps on a 3x3 grid `radius` texels apart, each itself a 2x2 bilinear compare, so the kernel is a smooth tent and a texel's stair-step does not survive it (four taps at +/-1 texel left it visible on the canopy struts a hand's width from the eye). A facet facing away from the sun pays no tap at all. No per-pixel noise rotation, unlike the sun's map's Vogel disk -- a grain that stays put on a dashboard a metre from the eye reads as a texture, and this surface has none.

cockpitSelfShadow.description: Let the COCKPIT SHELL shadow ITSELF (DEV-323). Matt, 2026-09-23: "in first person, i'd expect the cockpit to cast shadows on itself. like the bars should cast shadows on the console." The sun's map cannot: 2048 texels over a 1,400 m box is 0.68 m a texel, and a canopy bar is centimetres wide. So this is a SECOND map, over the shell's bounding sphere, cast by the shell (`ship_first_person`, which is the whole airframe with the canopy OPEN and its frame as bars) and sampled by the shell alone through one `onBeforeCompile` (`render/cockpit-self-shadow.ts`). The exterior hull is NOT a caster: its canopy is closed, opaque, near-black glass 0.33-0.43 m from the eye, hit by a ray from the eye in 720 of 720 directions 15-85 degrees up where the shell's frame stops 8.9 %, so in this map it would shade the whole cabin. TRUE ALSO CHANGES THE SUN'S MAP ON THE SHELL: the shell's lookup skips every occluder within the near box's own depth (`2 * radius` up-sun), because that same glass is look call 6's blob -- with `render.shipShadow` and `render.cockpitShadow` both on, it puts ~73 % of the visible cockpit in shade and no bar can show inside it. The near map answers the ship's shadow on itself; the sun's map keeps answering everything further away, including the ridge `render.cockpitShadow` exists for. INERT while `render.shadows` is off or at quality `low` (`cockpitSelfShadowEnabled` composes `shadowsEnabled`), which also puts it under the Advanced page's SHADOWS row. Inert on the JumpSeat, which has no shell by that name. A DEVIATION from 2016, whose cockpit neither cast nor received.

nearShadow.description: DEV-582, docs/plan/ULTRA.md. A second sun shadow map whose box follows the camera, hand-rolled beside the cockpit's (render/near-shadow.ts). Inside it the sun map's lookup skips the near map's up-sun reach, so the two maps are a cascade rather than a min of a sharp and a soft copy of one shadow. Casters and receivers are the sun map's, except the cockpit shell. Off wherever the sun map is off.

mapSize.description: Map edge in TEXELS, a power of two (`validateEdition` refuses anything else). The texel is `2 * boxHalfSize / mapSize`.

boxHalfSize.description: METRES, half the box on both axes across the sun, centred on the camera and snapped to the texel lattice. The up-sun reach is two of these, derived.

edgeFade.description: METRES inside the box's faces over which the near term and the sun map's skip fade together to nothing. Must be less than boxHalfSize.

bias.description: METRES of depth bias toward the light, normalised against the near box's own depth range at runtime (`shadowBiasFor`).

normalBias.description: METRES the receiver moves along its own normal before the lookup.

radius.description: PCF tap radius in near-map TEXELS (three's five-tap Vogel disk).

smoothSky.description: Bake the sky dome SMOOTH instead of faceted (DEV-320, wishlist #22a). TRUE on Anniversary (Matt, 2026-09-23: "faceted sky off by default"), FALSE on Classic. The flag names the deviation because the FACETED dome is the faithful answer: 2016's sky is `Quantum Theory/PolyWorld Skies/SkyJ.mat`, a low-poly pack whose six faces are flat polygons, a faceted horizon band and a hexagonal sun (`sim/sky-dome.ts`), so Classic keeps it off like every other flag (`tests/unit/edition-content.test.ts`). TRUE bakes BOTH domes -- the mission's and the title valley's -- with one colour per VERTEX, read off the same nine coefficients, cloud banks and sun glow, and no cell variation (`render/sky.ts`'s `bake`). The mesh, its draw order, its layer, its material and the sun cap do not change, so there is no new draw; the environment is prefiltered from the dome that is drawn, as it always is. NOT `scene.background`: DEV-307 tried that and the world vanished on Anniversary, because three draws its background box first in EVERY `renderer.render` call and bloom's UI pass is a second call over the finished frame (measured: with bloom off the same arm leaves the world drawn). Both domes are BUILT at this value; a flip at runtime re-bakes on the next frame.

sunHeight.description: Terrain shadow at EVERY distance: `sim/terrain/sun-height.ts` sweeps the collision height field once per mission along the sun's azimuth and stores, per texel, the height below which a point is in terrain shadow. Uploaded as one R16F texture; every lit material takes min(shadow map, this) inside the map's box and this alone beyond it. The fix for a far island reading lit and a near one shadowed (DEV-116).

softMetres.description: METRES of height over which a lit fragment fades to shadowed across the swept top (a GLSL smoothstep centred on it). The collision field has none of the render mesh's +-1.3 m jitter, so 0 is a legal hard step that stairs along every facet; 3 covers the jitter with a metre to spare. DEV-116.

cloudShadow.description: DEV-585, docs/plan/ULTRA.md. The clouds' shadows on everything lit. `render/cloud-shadow.ts` projects the live cloud placements (the scale and lift in force) along the mission sun onto the plane y = 0 once per mission, into an RG16F map of (coverage, highest cloud on that sun ray), and `render/far-shadow.ts`'s `ff2SunHeightTerm` multiplies the sun by it, so the ground, the sea, the props, the racers, the cockpit and the sea's glint all take it. Projecting along the sun rather than to one layer height is exact at any sun angle; the wind is a uniform offset. The clouds themselves do not receive it.

strength.description: How much of the DIRECT sun a cloud takes away: the sun is multiplied by `1 - strength` under a cloud. 0 is no shadow; 1 is as dark as a terrain shadow (the sky and ambient light are never touched).

minSunElevation.description: DEGREES. The term is off at or below this sun elevation and full at twice it (a smoothstep between), so a sun on the horizon does not stretch every cloud across the map. 0 means no fade above the horizon.

canopyShade.description:
Baked contact darkening under the prop scatter: `sim/props/canopy.ts` sweeps every DRAWN prop onto the land's own collision grid once per mission and records, per texel, how much sky the canopy above it takes away. It rides the spare channel of DEV-116's sun texture, so it costs no second fetch, and it multiplies the light after `aomap_fragment` -- on the LAND flat, and on the PROPS ramped out as their own fragments rise past the canopy ceiling over them, so a lone tree's crown stays lit (DEV-296). Not on the sea, the racers, the ship or the cockpit. Wishlist #13, DEV-295 and DEV-296.

It is a RESTORATION rather than a new effect, and that is why it may touch the DIRECT sun as well as the ambient. When DEV-295 landed, `render.props.scatterShadows` was false on both presets (DEV-224 — the scatter is 88-93 % of desert's and alpine's world pass), so a tree cast nothing on the ground it stands on, and Matt's report was exactly that: "the grass under thick forests is the same color as an open field." Nothing else darkened that ground, so there was no live shadow to double.

DEV-304 MADE THAT PREMISE CONDITIONAL rather than true, and the INDIRECT half is unaffected: the shadow map never touches ambient or hemisphere light, so this bake is the only thing darkening it whatever the caster set says. The DIRECT half is weighted by `render/shadows.ts`'s `canopyDirectWeight` — 1 while the scatter casts nothing, 0 once it does — which is composed from `shadowCastersFor` and therefore right at quality `low` and inside a headset without knowing about either. It reaches the shader as a uniform (`uSunTopD.z`), so a live flip on the Advanced page moves it in the same frame with no program recompile. Turning this flag off still produces exactly the pre-DEV-295 image; turning `props.scatterShadows` off still produces exactly the DEV-295 image.

radiusScale.description: Canopy radius as a multiple of the prop's DRAWN half-width. 1 darkens exactly the ground the prop covers; above 1 spreads past the silhouette, which is what contact darkening looks like, because the light that reaches the edge has come a long way sideways. Since DEV-297 it sets the SIZE of the contact patch and no longer its depth — the kernel peaks at a full unit whatever the radius, so widening it no longer makes every tree's shade fainter.

saturation.description: The COVERAGE at which 63 % of the sky is gone — `occlusion = 1 - exp(-coverage / saturation)`, the transmittance of a uniform medium. Lower is a darker forest. In `sim/props/canopy.ts`'s own units, measured there rather than guessed: since DEV-297 one canopy overhead is exactly 1, so this reads directly — at 1, a lone tree takes 1 - 1/e = 63 % of `strength` from the ground under it and three overlapping take 95 %. Lower makes a single tree darker; higher needs a thicket before anything shows.

strength.description: How dark the most occluded ground gets, 0..1. 0 is the exact current image, which is what makes this safe to ship before anyone has flown it; 1 would be black ground under a thicket. The sweep folds this in, so a preset at 0 produces a field of exact zeroes and the upload is skipped.

skyVisibility.description: DEV-333, docs/plan/SKY-VISIBILITY.md. The terrain shading the sky it hides, and lighting the shade it throws. `sim/terrain/sky-visibility.ts` bakes, once per world, how much of each facet's sky the terrain hides (V, relative to the facet's own plane, so a slope in open country is untouched) and the one-bounce light of the sunlit terrain doing the hiding (B). `render/sky-visibility.ts` reads both at the facet's barycentre uv, one value per face, and acts on the LAND's indirect light only; DEV-116 owns the sun. Matt, 2026-09-23: "right now the shadows are very dark" and "mesa canyon is a good example". V alone only darkens, which is why bounce leads.

sky.description: How far the probe is mixed toward V: `indirect *= mix(1, V, sky)`. 0 leaves the sky light alone. SKY-VISIBILITY 6a: the colour maps already paint 5 % (desert) to 46 % (kauai) of this darkening into the albedo, so a high value double-darkens kauai and alpine.

bounce.description: How much of the lit terrain's one-bounce light is added: `indirect += bounce * B * sunColour * BRDF_Lambert(albedo)`. 1 is the physical amount for a Lambertian bounce off the colour map's albedo. 0 adds nothing.

horizonGeo.description: A far shore of paper-cut ridges where the sea met the sky in a line: two bands of flat one-colour cards round the eye, at `radius` metres, coloured from the mission's own sky at the horizon and darkened by `silhouette`, fogged by the mission fog, one draw call. 2016 had nothing here (gameplay video 9:25, `f0565`). king-tide's horizon ring is the placement idea. DEV-119.

radius.description: METRES from the eye to the outer band. Must clear the 6,000 m far plane from the highest seat and sit past the island; `int_01` can put the island's far hills ~6 km away from the boundary's far side, where a ring inside that passes through them (DEV-119 section 4).

peakMetres.description: METRES the tallest card stands above the reference level (sea level, or a valley floor). 0 is a ring that is all under water — a legal no-op.

silhouette.description: Multiplier on the sky's horizon colour behind each card. 1 is the sky itself (invisible against it); 0.55 is a cut-out in shade. The one colour number, and it is a ratio of the mission's sky rather than a colour of its own.

shallowDepth.description:
METRES of water. At and beyond this depth the sea is untouched; at zero it is `shallowStrength` of the way to `shallowColor`, linear between. The shader is handed 1/this, so it may not be zero.

WHAT THE NUMBER BUYS IS A BAND WIDTH, and the band width is the bathymetry's, not ours: Simonet's coastline is 25.06 km long and its shore runs at roughly 1:1, so the mean horizontal width of the 0..D band (area over perimeter, measured on a 4 m grid against a 116.6 m waterline) is 1.5 m at D = 4, 8.5 m at 16, 34.7 m at 50 and 57.8 m at 70. 50 puts the shallows about one OCEAN facet wide at `?ocean=8` — the smallest thing the sea's own geometry can express.

shallowStrength.description: 0..1. How far toward `shallowColor` at zero depth. 0 is no shift at any depth, which is the identity whatever the flag says.

shallowColor.description: sRGB 0..1, the way `fog.color` in a level and `haze.tint` both are. Linearised in `render/coast.ts` by the same `srgbToLinear` everything else uses, because it ends up mixed against a linear framebuffer. 2016's open sea is (43, 130, 247) in every texel of `water_color` — a single flat blue — so this is the only colour variation the water has ever had.

foamDepth.description: METRES. Foam lives strictly inside (0, this), brightest at the waterline. Same reciprocal, same floor. On Simonet's 1:1 shore, 16 is a mean band of 8.5 m — about one LAND facet — and 4 would be 1.5 m, which is a fifth of a facet and would never be seen.

foamStrength.description: 0..1. Peak foam at the waterline. START FAINT: ANNIVERSARY.md section 6 records king-tide's overlays being authored at demo strength, reading as 'allover noise' on a lap, and being dialled to near zero and then removed.

foamColor.description: sRGB 0..1. An ALBEDO, not a light — it is mixed into `diffuseColor` before the lighting, so a value of 1 is white water rather than a white pixel, and the 4-degree sun still shades it.

foamBreakup.description: 0..1. How much of the foam the CHOP takes away, so the band reads as broken water rather than as a drawn outline. The modulator is the game's own wave, evaluated per FRAGMENT (`coastChop` in `render/water.ts`) — 11.1 m of wavelength and a 3.14 s period, which the 256 m mesh has never been able to carry and a pixel can. It reads the wave; it does not change it, and the 23x undersample stays the FINDING it is. 0 is an unbroken band.

coast.description: The shoreline: a depth-driven shallows colour and a foam line at the waterline, both read from the ISLAND's own height map through the same `importUnityTexture` path the land was generated from. 2016 had a flat colour map, a 256 m plate and a hard line at the join. ANNIVERSARY.md section 1.3 item 5, section 1.5 item 5, V6, and DEV-087.

seaReflection.description: DEV-583, docs/plan/ULTRA.md. 2016's realtime sea reflection (Water.mat's V_LP_REFLECTIVE_REALTIME), restored on a MONITOR under the ultra tier only: `render/sea-reflection.ts` renders a camera mirrored through the sea plane (an oblique near plane at the water) into a target, and `render/water.ts` reads it at the fragment's screen position pushed by the facet normal, composited over the sky reflection. Needs this flag AND the ultra tier in force, which is never true in a headset. The tint, strength, Fresnel and push are the sheet's (`reflection` on the ocean's material), not this block's.

resolutionScale.description: The mirror target's size as a fraction of the drawing buffer, per axis. 0.5 is half resolution (a quarter of the pixels); 1 is the full frame.

base.description:
The RESTING lens, in degrees of VERTICAL field of view, or `null` for the renderer's own — 70, from `src/render/renderer.ts`, which is about 102 degrees horizontal at 16:9.

BOTH presets ship `null`, and that is a decision rather than an omission. ANNIVERSARY.md section 1.5 item 8 argues that 70 is a very wide lens, that wide lenses minify the middle distance, and that 55-60 would make the world FEEL larger on a monitor at some cost to the sense of speed. That is one number, it is the creative director's (hard rule 9), and every A/B frame ever taken of this game would move with it — so the key exists, `?lookdev=1` has a live slider on it to feel the answer, and until somebody feels it the shipped value is the port's own. Never reaches a headset: in session the projection comes from the XRView. DEV-093.

addBySpeed.description:
Airspeed in m/s -> DEGREES ADDED to `base`. A delta and not a multiplier, so moving `base` does not silently rescale the effect.

x is `Ship_HoverShip.ForwardSpeed`, the same quantity the particles, the wind curves and the cockpit shake are keyed on — NOT a boost stage. `Boost_FOV.cs` was named for the boost and a stage would be the literal port, but a boost IS a speed rise: one curve then captures the boost, the speed chain, a dive and a valley tailwind, all of which are the lens opening for the same reason, and nothing in `game/flight.ts` has to expose a stage to read it.

The breakpoints are the game's own speeds, off the generated sheet: 90 is `derived.hoverjet.terminalSpeedCruise` (89.8115, the unboosted thrust/drag fixed point, and ANNIVERSARY.md section 2.1's '90 m/s'), 120 is `hoverjet.ship.minBoostEffectsSpeed`, 180 is `derived.hoverjet.terminalSpeedBoost` (179.6229, exactly twice cruise), 240 is `minBoostEffect_stage2_speed`, and 340 is where the S4 audio curves stop. Zero at 90 is load-bearing: at cruise the lens is EXACTLY the authored one, so every existing A/B frame of a cruising ship is unchanged and the effect is a change signal rather than a new baseline.

attackSeconds.description: SECONDS: the time constant while the lens OPENS. Not a duration — after this long the remaining gap is down by 1/e (63 % of the way), after three of them it is 95 % closed. `1 - exp(-dt / tau)` rather than a per-frame lerp factor, so the feel is the same on a 72 Hz headset-mirror and a 144 Hz monitor. A hole here is an infinite exponent and an instant snap: a feature that works and has no feel, with nothing in the console, which is why `validateEdition` refuses a non-positive value.

releaseSeconds.description: SECONDS: the time constant while it CLOSES. Slower than the attack, which is the one thing `Boost_FOV.cs` settles — it grows its lerp parameter at `speed` on the way out and at `speed * 0.8` on the way back, a ratio of 1.25. This preset is more asymmetric than that on purpose: the moment that reads badly is the lens snapping shut when you lift off for a gate, and the settle is where the whole 'that was fast' feeling lives. The ratio is a number to argue with.

flatFov.description:
A wider lens with speed, on the FLAT build ONLY. 2016 shipped NO fov effect — `Boost_FOV.cs` exists, and its guid `61d3a179f37ff424996da53f65441764` appears in exactly one text file in the whole Unity project: its own `.cs.meta`, where the guid is defined. No prefab and no scene references it, and nothing sets its `increaseFOV`. So this is FF2's own feature with a 2015 script as its brief, which is why it is Anniversary-only and has a row.

FORBIDDEN IN VR, and it is the only block here with a place it must not run: research 05 section R7 says never write `camera.fov` while presenting, because a projection that disagrees with the compositor's lens assumptions warps the periphery and is a direct nausea trigger. `render/flat-fov.ts` returns before it reads anything while `renderer.xr.isPresenting`, and restores the base at BOTH ends of a session — the second one because three writes `camera.fov` itself in session, back-derived from the XRView (`three.module.js:14676`), so without the restore taking the headset off would leave the flat build on the headset's ~96-degree lens.

And it is NOT scaled by the `speedFx` comfort slider, unlike S1, S2, S3 and S6 — ANNIVERSARY.md section 2.6 lists those four and not this one. DEV-093 carries the argument and names the one line that would change it. ANNIVERSARY.md S7, DEV-093.

wrap.description: 0..1. Half-Lambert WRAP of the direct diffuse, so the terminator is soft: 0 is the hard edge three gives a solid and 1 is `(N.L + 1) / 2`, light rolling all the way round to the far side. NOT a stylisation — `render/cloud-look.ts` adds the DIFFERENCE between a wrapped Lambert and three's own hard one, in three's own units and through three's own 1/pi, so the total is exactly the wrapped form. 0 is the identity in the exact sense: both halves saturate, so the two cancel float for float.

rimStrength.description: Peak rim at the silhouette, in the SAME units as the wrap — 1 is about what a fully sunlit face receives, so this is readable as a fraction of one. An opaque body with a bright edge rather than a transparency pass, because overdraw in VR is V5's named risk and nineteen alpha-blended bodies of up to 893 m are several full-screen layers of fill on a Quest.

rimPower.description: Fresnel exponent on `1 - N.V`. Higher is a thinner edge: 2 is a broad light-wrap over most of the body, 5 is a rim you would call a rim, 12 is a hairline. Never zero — `x^0` is 1, which would be a full-strength rim over the whole cloud.

sunTint.description: 0..1. How far the added light takes the SUN's own colour rather than a neutral of the same luminance (Rec. 709, the same weights `render/haze.ts` desaturates toward and for the same reason). 1 is the physically exact wrap; below 1 keeps the crown whiter than a 4-degree sunset would paint it, which is an art choice and is why it is a knob. The sun colour itself is NOT here: it comes from the mission's `lighting.sun`, because the sun is per-mission and not per-environment, and a colour in this file would light every mission's clouds the same.

emissive.description: `MeshStandardMaterial.emissiveIntensity` on the cloud's own colour — the flat floor that stops a 4-degree sun leaving the underside black. 0.22 is FF2's own and is what BOTH presets shipped before this row (DEV-028), so Classic's 0.22 is the identity rather than a no-op zero. Anniversary lifts it because the wrap fills the TERMINATOR and the deepest faces, which point away from the sun entirely, still have only this and the IBL.

scaleMultiplier.description: Multiplies 2016's authored scale on ALL THREE axes, so the flattening survives (y is 40-50 % of x in the placements and a shape that squashed as well would squash twice — `sim/clouds.ts`'s `flatten` note). 1 is 2016 exactly, which is what 'faithful placement stays in Classic' means. On `int_01_hoverJet` the nineteen run 181.7 m to 893.2 m across, mean 513.5.

altitudeLift.description: METRES added to every cloud's y. 0 is 2016. On `int_01_hoverJet` the nineteen sit at 539 m to 1,382 m (mean 1,074) over a course that runs 134 m to 890 m, so a lift raises the layer relative to the flying without touching the terrain.

driftSpeed.description: METRES PER SECOND along `driftDirection`, on the RENDER clock — wall time, like the waves and DEV-089's flocks, because a cloud is ambience and nothing under `src/sim/` can see one. 0 is 2016's still sky. A pure function of the clock rather than an integrator, so a dropped frame costs nothing; and `?snap=` does NOT freeze it (docs/vr-testing.md section 5), so an A/B pair differs by a few metres of drift.

driftDirection.description: Direction of travel in THREE space, normalised by `render/cloud-look.ts` so it need not be a unit vector. A y component is legal and means the layer slowly rises.

singleSided.description: DEV-276. Cull the cloud's BACK faces. false is what the port has always drawn -- DoubleSide, so a lobed blob does not show holes between its knots at a grazing angle -- and is Classic's answer. true means a cloud you are INSIDE draws nothing, because every face between you and the world is a back face; that is both halves of Matt's 'the cloud geo would be hidden (or at least not double-sided)' for one line and no per-frame test. Read even when `enabled` is false: this is not part of V5's look, it is which faces the mesh has.

whiteout.description: DEV-277. The cloud whiteout level, 0-1, and 0 is off. Matt: 'fade to white immediately when entering and softly fade out when you exit.' Instant in, linear out over whiteoutRelease. This is what singleSided made room for: the opaque hull WAS doing this by accident, and it could not be tuned, could not have an onset, and showed its own facets through itself.

poolSize.description: DEV-785. The cloud variant pool: the TOTAL number of unique blobs the sky builds, each one InstancedMesh, shared out over the shapes by what the placements ask for (game/cloud-pool.ts). A pool at least as big as the sky shares nothing and every placement keeps the blob it always had. Read when the sky is BUILT, even when enabled is false, and not pushed again on a preset flip: a pool is geometry.

tintSpread.description: DEV-785. How far a placement that SHARES a pool member strays from the authored cloud colour, as a fraction: its albedo is multiplied by 1 plus this times a deterministic value in -1..1. 0 is no tint. A placement that owns its member is never tinted. Read when the sky is built, like poolSize.

whiteoutRelease.description: DEV-277. Seconds to fade the whiteout out on EXIT. Entry is instant by design -- a cloud boundary is a surface you cross in one frame at 90 m/s, and easing in reads as the fog arriving late, which is the complaint this replaces. Linear rather than exponential so it actually reaches 0; an exponential would leave every frame after a cloud very slightly milky for ever.

clouds.description: Clouds that are clouds: a half-Lambert wrap so the terminator is soft, a fresnel rim where the sun is behind them, drift, and 2016's placements grown. ANNIVERSARY.md section 1.3 item 4 (*'the clouds read as boulders'*), section 1.5 item 4, V5, and DEV-090. No transparency pass and no shadow casting: at a 4-degree sun a cloud's shadow lands ten kilometres down-sun, which is why C1 was dropped.

threshold.description: Rec.709 LUMINANCE, in LINEAR light, above which a pixel glows — the same quantity 2016's `BloomOptimized.threshold` was, and 2016's number was 0.63. It carries over unchanged because the domain does: Unity 5 wrote linear radiance to an LDR framebuffer where 1.0 is clipping white and ran the image effect on that, and the composer's target holds linear radiance with the same white point (three applies `renderer.toneMapping` only when the destination is the canvas or an XR target, `three.module.js:7551`, so `OutputPass` puts ACES on at the END). What DID change is how much energy sits above it — 2016 clipped at 1.0 and a HalfFloat target does not — which is why `strength` is not 2016's `intensity`. DEV-091.

strength.description: `UnrealBloomPass.strength`, and NOT 2016's `intensity: 0.53`. three composites `bloom = 3.0 * strength * sum(lerpBloomFactor(f_i) * mip_i)` and adds it, and at `radius` 0 the five weights sum to 3.0 — so for a bright region larger than every kernel the added light is `9 * strength * L`, and the strength that matches 2016's `intensity * L` there is 0.53/9 = 0.059. That figure is a FLOOR, not the answer: a ring stud, the sun disc and a speed streak are all far smaller than the five kernels (12 to about 1,400 frame pixels across), so the same strength delivers much less at the things we want to glow. THE NUMBER TO ARGUE WITH, against the same-tick A/B frames.

radius.description: 0..1: how much of the glow lives in the WIDE mips, not a distance and not pixels. `lerpBloomFactor(f) = mix(f, 1.2 - f, radius)`, so 0 leaves the weights at [1, .8, .6, .4, .2] — the half-res mip dominating, a tight glow — and 1 inverts them to [.2, .4, .6, .8, 1], the 1/32-res mip dominating, a wide soft halo. 2016 ran ONE blur iteration at `blurSize 1.2` on its own downsampled buffer, i.e. a tight glow and not a halo, so the faithful shape is a LOW number.

resolutionScale.description: Multiplies the drawing-buffer size the bloom CHAIN is built at. `UnrealBloomPass.setSize` halves whatever it is handed before the first mip (`UnrealBloomPass.js:250-262`), so 1 is ALREADY the half-resolution bloom ANNIVERSARY.md section 3.2 asked for and 0.5 starts the chain at a quarter. It is the Quest lever if the VR variant ever happens, and the only bloom key that is a texture size rather than a uniform — changing it resizes six render targets.

vrHalo.description: DEV-336. Bloom in a HEADSET, the cheap way ANNIVERSARY.md V2 wrote down and never built: additive halo billboards on the gate studs (one instanced draw sharing the studs' own instance matrix) and on the sun (one quad), no post pass. Drawn only while presenting and only when `enabled` is on, so the monitor keeps the real bloom above and Classic gets neither. Matt, 2026-09-23: "i also didn't see bloom working in vr" and "if there's a cheap way to do it, let's do it."

studRadius.description: A stud halo's radius as a multiple of that stud's own mean scale, so it shrinks with a passed gate. 0 draws nothing.

studIntensity.description: Peak additive brightness at a stud halo's centre, in the studs' extracted glow colour, falling off as (1 - r^2)^2.

sunAngleDeg.description: The sun halo's radius as an angle at the eye, degrees.

sunIntensity.description: Peak additive brightness at the sun halo's centre, in the mission sun's own colour.

bloom.description: Bloom: on a monitor the real post pass below, from 2016's own five numbers; in a HEADSET the `vrHalo` billboards instead (DEV-336), because the post pass never composites while presenting. `EffectComposer` = `RenderPass` + `UnrealBloomPass` + `OutputPass` into a HalfFloat MSAA target, never while `renderer.xr.isPresenting` — a post pass in stereo forfeits the compositor path the frame budget assumes (PORT_PLAN section 6.1, R6). Which is also what 2016 did: the component sat on `Main Camera` under `Mono_Cam`, and `CameraMode.cs` boots with `vrMode = true`, so the headset never saw it. `render/bloom.ts` carries the whole trace. The UI is exempt by the same line `render/tone.ts` draws, enforced as a LAYER split rather than by `material.toneMapped`, because that flag means nothing inside a render target. ANNIVERSARY.md V2, DEV-091.

armLength.description: METRES from the pivot to the camera along the lagged arm, before any shortening — Unreal's `TargetArmLength`. The one number to argue with: 2016's GearVR `3rdPerson_Ship.prefab` authors its `target_cam` 8.35 m behind and 1.56 m above the ship (never in the Steam build), and the 2016 Steam screenshots of that mode read as 25-35 m once its per-frame position lerp has fallen behind at 150 m/s. DEV-128.

minArmLength.description: METRES. The probe never shortens the arm below this, so a camera pinned against a cliff still sees a ship and not the inside of a hull.

pivotOffset.description: [x, y, z] METRES from the SHIP ORIGIN in the ship's frame as three sees it (−z forward, +y up): where the arm hangs from — Unreal's `TargetOffset`, with the socket at the ship. Not `metres3`, which is from the EYE; a third-person camera has no eye to be relative to.

armPitchDeg.description: DEGREES the arm is raised above the ship's lagged horizon. Positive puts the camera above and behind, looking down the arm at the pivot; 0 is level with the ship.

aimPitchDeg.description: DEGREES of extra camera pitch relative to the arm. Negative aims the lens below the pivot, which LIFTS the ship in the frame — the 2016 screenshots have it about a third down from the top, and this is the knob that puts it there.

positionLagSeconds.description: SECONDS: the time constant of the pivot's position lag, `1 - exp(-dt / tau)` like `flatFov` — Unreal's `CameraLagSpeed` is the reciprocal. The arm origin trails the ship by this much, which is what makes acceleration and a boost VISIBLE from outside.

rotationLagSeconds.description: SECONDS: the time constant of the arm's rotation lag (Unreal's `CameraRotationLagSpeed`, reciprocal). Slower than the position lag on purpose: a camera that turns as fast as the ship shows a ship that never appears to turn.

maxLagMetres.description: METRES the lagged pivot may fall behind the true one before it is clamped — Unreal's `CameraLagMaxDistance`. Without it a boost from rest leaves the ship out of frame for a second.

pitchFollow.description: 0..1: how much of the ship's PITCH the arm inherits. 1 dives with the nose; 0 keeps the arm level and lets the ship pitch inside the frame.

rollFollow.description: 0..1: how much of the ship's BANK the horizon tilts by — the Riders Republic cue the triage page names. 0 is the `?view=chase` photography tool's world-up camera; 1 is rigidly welded to a ship that banks 45 degrees through a gate, which is unwatchable.

probeRadius.description: METRES of clearance kept between the camera and the collision surface (terrain OR sea) along the arm — Unreal's `ProbeSize`. The arm is shortened to the first sample that would sink the lens within this of the ground.

fovAddBySpeed.description: Airspeed in m/s -> DEGREES added to the resting lens while this camera is live, SCALED BY the speed-FX comfort slider (0 / 0.5 / 1). Zero at the slider's minimum by construction, and the unit test says so. Unlike `render.flatFov` this one IS on the slider: seen from outside the ship the widening lens is pure optic flow with no cockpit frame to anchor it (ANNIVERSARY.md section 2.6). The x breakpoints are the same sheet speeds `flatFov.addBySpeed` uses.

hudOffset.description: [x, y, z] METRES from the CAMERA, camera frame (−z forward), where the cockpit readout is re-parented while this camera is live — a screen-space plate, which is how 2016's GearVR third-person screenshots carry the same three plates along the bottom of the frame. Flat build only, so a head-locked plate costs nothing.

hudScale.description: The readout's scale on the lens. 1 is the cockpit's 0.4 m panel at `hudOffset`'s distance.

thirdPerson.description: A player-switchable third-person camera in the manner of Unreal's SpringArm: a pivot on the ship, an arm with a lagged position and a separately lagged rotation, shortened when the terrain or the sea would occlude the ship, the horizon tilting with bank, and a lens that opens with speed on the comfort slider. The pad's X (InControl `Action3` — 2016's own CHANGE VIEW binding, `Input_Ship.cs:312`), V on the keyboard and the CAM chip toggle it. NEVER in an XR session: a rig-relative third person in a headset is a comfort feature of its own and is not this one. **2016 DID ship a third-person view**: both `PlayerShip_SR14_Photon.prefab` and `JumpSeat_Photon.prefab` carry `CamChanger` with a `CamRoot_3rdPerson` target, rigidly parented, no lag, no probe — that camera is on the sheet (`hoverjet.camera.thirdPerson`, `jumpseat.camera.thirdPerson`) and is what the toggle gives on Classic. `enabled` here switches on the SPRING — the lag, the probe, the bank follow and the lens term — which 2016 did not have. DEV-128.

palette.description: One colour per AI racer, in racer order (the two 2016 pads first, then `gameplay.racers.slots`), WRAPPING past the end: the colour of the livery's main PANEL, sRGB 0..1, in the units 2016's FBX carries. Each racer's orange is turned onto it in HSL relative to the player's panel (`render/racer-livery.ts`), so its shades keep their places. READ AT LOAD, on both presets: it is what a flip to Anniversary paints, and it is the colour `__ff2.racers()` reports on each racer's spec (`colour`, `#rrggbb`) for a minimap or a results row to reuse. The title screen's two flypast jets take the first two.

shadow.description: The solid hulls CAST into the sun's map, as the player's hull does (`shadowFlagsFor`'s `racer-hull` row: cast, never receive). Composed with `render.racerLivery.enabled` in `shadowCastersFor`, so a hologram never casts, and with `shadowsEnabled`, so it is INERT while `render.shadows` is off or at quality `low`. Its own feature path so `vr.disable` can take the shadow without the look.

racerLivery.description: DEV-350. Matt, 2026-09-24: "replace ai 'ghosts' as ai 'racers' - solid shaded, different coloration than the player's orange hoverjet." TRUE: every AI racer wears the player's own hull and material (`lambert1`), opaque and lit, with the livery in its VERTEX COLOURS turned to its own palette colour. That is 2016's `GhostRacer.prefab` -- `hoverJet_exterior_blue.fbx` under the player's `lambert1.mat`, opaque, casting -- and not its playback ghost. FALSE: 2016's ghost look, which the port's racers wore until DEV-350 -- one translucent emissive blue for every racer (`racerMaterial`). Followed live on a flip; the palette is read at load. The wing's glow is the same in both (DEV-322). Not the sim: nothing here moves a racer.

color.description: sRGB 0..1, as a colour picker gives it. Only its HUE and SATURATION matter: the gain is this divided by its own Rec. 709 luma, so a neutral pixel keeps its brightness and white is no tint at any strength.

strength.description: 0 is no tint whatever the colour; 1 is the whole of it.

default.description: The tint of every level `missions` does not name. Neutral as shipped on both presets.

missions.description: By level id (`content/levels/<id>.json`, or an authored course's id), each `{ color, strength }` in the shape of `default`. This schema's validator cannot type the values of a free-keyed object, so `validateEdition` checks each one at load and names the key; `edition-content.test.ts` checks every key is a real level. Empty as shipped: nothing is tinted until Matt authors a row with `?lookdev=1`.

sceneTint.description: DEV-446. A colour filter over the displayed world, authored per MISSION. 2016 had no scene-wide tint on any camera in any shipped scene (DEV-446 has the walk), so Classic has it OFF, and Anniversary ships it ON with a neutral `default` and no `missions`: not a pixel moves until one is authored. Per channel the world is multiplied by mix(1, color / luma(color), strength), clamped to 0..2 -- a luma-preserving filter on the tone-mapped, encoded frame, which is what makes it one filter on the composite, in a headset and on Classic alike (`render/scene-tint.ts`). Drawn as one blended full-screen quad and only while not identity. Not in `gameplay`: it moves no ship and restarts no board.

widthScale.description: Multiplies the streak's rendered WIDTH and nothing else. The authored 5-8 cm is a 1-2 px hairline; about 5 puts it at 0.25-0.4 m, which is the range the eye can measure at 100 m. The streak's LENGTH, its speed, its rate and its lifetime stay exactly as `HOVERJET.particles` has them — they are generated, and S2 re-authors only what the eye can measure. DEV-079.

alphaScale.description: Multiplies the particle alpha after the authored gradient. 1 is 2016.

softEdge.description: Swap the hard triangle matte for a soft-edged streak laid OVER the background instead of added to it. Additive white cannot darken, so on 2016's bright mauve sky an additive streak has nowhere to go — this is what lets `coreDarkness` mean anything. False is 2016.

coreDarkness.description: 0-1. How dark the streak's centre line goes, so the flanks read against dark terrain and the core reads against a bright sky. Needs `softEdge`. 0 is 2016.

tubeLift.description: METRES the three boost tubes are lifted toward the eye, in the ship frame. 2016 authors their axis at (0, -5.6, 100) under Effects/shipOffset — 6.6 m BELOW the eye — so at stage 1 (shell radius 4.63 m) the whole tube runs under the cockpit floor and only its far end is visible; the 40 s same-tick A/B frames showed exactly that. 6.6 centres it on the eye: stage 1 rings the canopy at 4.6 m, stages 2-3 at 8 m. A transform on the emitter, never a change to the generated spec; scaled by the comfort slider like the width. 0 is 2016. DEV-079, second pass.

speedLines.description: 2016's four speed-driven particle systems are ALWAYS drawn — they are the shipped game. `enabled` re-authors only what the eye can measure (width, alpha, a soft edge and a dark core) so the streaks read instead of rendering as hairlines. ANNIVERSARY.md S2, DEV-079.

onsetSpeed.description: Metres per second of FORWARD speed at which the first boost stage starts to emit. Its rate, alpha and spawn speed then rise together and reach 2016's own numbers at the middle of stage 1's band ((120 + 240) / 2 off the sheet). At or above that middle the ramp-in degenerates to a step there. The only speed in the ramp that is not 2016's.

alphaFloor.description: The alpha multiplier the first streaks are born at, rising to 1 at the middle of stage 1's band. Multiplies S2's `alphaScale`, never replaces it.

speedFloor.description: The spawn-speed multiplier the first streaks are born at, rising to 1 at the middle of stage 1's band. The engine draws a streak's length from its velocity, so this is the stretch as well. Stage 1 is emitted about 100 m ahead of the eye, so a low floor means streaks that die before they reach you.

speedRamp.description: The speed lines RAMP instead of switching. 2016 plays exactly one of the three boost systems at a time, cut at the prefab's 120 / 240 / 350 m/s; `enabled` crossfades them by emission rate instead, each stage 2016's own and alone at the middle of its band, and ramps the first one in, in count, alpha and speed. No multiplier exceeds the generated spec. Off at the speed-FX comfort slider's 0, like S2; drawn whole above it. DEV-351.

seconds.description: Seconds a point of vapour lives: the ribbon is this long times the forward speed (0.3 s is 54 m at 180 m/s).

startWidth.description: Metres across the whole glow (core and halo) at the tip.

endWidth.description: Metres across the whole glow at the tail, where the alpha reaches nothing. Wider than the start: the vapour spreads as it thins.

alpha.description: Opacity at the tip at whole strength, authored at the speed-FX slider's `full`: the slider multiplies it (light, the default, is half). Falls linearly to nothing over `seconds`.

minVertexDistance.description: Metres a tip travels before a point is committed, as a Unity TrailRenderer's `minVertexDistance`.

nearFade.description: Metres from the eye inside which the ribbon fades out: nothing AT the eye, whole at this distance, a smoothstep between. For a ribbon passing through the eye (in a headset, a racer's vapour across your face). The chase view's width is `maxWidthDeg`'s job, not this: at 10 m this also faded the whole of the player's own trail, which is all within ~7 m of the chase camera. 0 is no fade.

tint.description: How far each craft's trail is drawn from white toward its own livery's hue at FULL BRIGHTNESS: a racer's palette colour (DEV-350), the player's orange panel. 0 is white. The livery is divided by its brightest channel before it is mixed, so the trail takes its hue and saturation and never its darkness: no channel falls below 1 - tint, and charcoal, which has no hue, stays white. DEV-358 follow-up.

glow.description: The centre line's brightness, LINEAR, times the tint: an HDR colour. Above render.bloom.threshold (1.0) at the default slider is what makes the flat bloom catch it; in a headset, where bloom never composites, it is tone-mapped per material to near-white over the halo.

core.description: The bright core's half-width as a fraction of the whole glow's. The ribbon is five vertices across: edge, core edge, centre, core edge, edge.

halo.description: The brightness at the core's edge as a fraction of the centre's; from there the halo falls to nothing at the glow's edge. The halo is geometry, so a headset, which has no bloom, still sees a glow.

maxWidthDeg.description: Degrees: the widest the ribbon may subtend at the eye. From the chase seat the player's trail streams back past the camera, 3-7 m away, and at its world width that is a band 20-40 px wide from the frame's corners; the cap keeps it a thin bright line. 0 is no cap.

fromCockpit.description: Whether the PLAYER's own trails show from the cockpit seat. False: third person only. The racers' show from every view.

wingTrails.description: Wing-tip trails at speed, on the player's ship (in third person, and from the seat when `fromCockpit` says so) and on every AI racer. Two thin ribbons per HoverJet from the tips' trailing corners, measured off the hull. They fade in by smoothstep and are whole at the HoverJet's unboosted terminal speed (`derived.hoverjet.terminalSpeedCruise`, 89.8 m/s), from nothing the boost's own factor below it (cruise squared over `terminalSpeedBoost`, 44.9), both off the sheet; the speed-FX comfort slider multiplies `alpha` and its 0 is off. Each craft's trail is lightly tinted toward its own livery and glows: an HDR core the flat bloom catches, and a halo in the ribbon's own geometry for a headset. One draw for all the racers, one for the player. DEV-358, and its follow-up.

count.description: Pool size at speed FX `full`. The player's comfort slider multiplies it (0 / 0.5 / 1), so this is a ceiling and not a promise. One draw call however big it is; the budget is about 2000.

innerRadius.description: Metres from the EYE that a mote may first appear. The canopy is 1-2 m out, so anything under about 3 spawns inside the cockpit, which in a headset is not air but a fault.

outerRadius.description: Metres. The shell's outside; a mote past it respawns. Radii are drawn log-uniformly between the two, which is equal counts per octave of distance — a linear draw would put almost every mote at the far edge, where optic flow is exactly the thing the game already has too much of.

size.description: Metres across. A few centimetres: at 3 m that is a degree, which is a fleck rather than a snowflake.

stretchSeconds.description: Seconds of travel drawn as length: length = size + this * relative speed. At 0.006 a mote is 0.3 m at 40 m/s (a speck) and 1.1 m at 180 (a short streak).

alpha.description: Peak alpha, reached at `fullSpeed`, BEFORE the comfort slider multiplies it.

minSpeed.description: Metres per second below which the field draws nothing. Deliberately NOT 2016's 25 m/s effects threshold, which is a generated constant and belongs to the shipped systems.

fullSpeed.description: Metres per second at which alpha reaches `alpha`. Between the two it ramps.

aheadBias.description: 0-1. How much of the shell sits ahead of the velocity: 0 spawns uniformly around the eye and 1 spawns only in front. A mote behind you is a mote you will never meet, and it respawns on the next frame anyway.

colorLight.description: Linear RGB. Each mote takes a shade somewhere between this and `colorDark`, so part of the field always has contrast with whatever is behind it — bright sky or dark terrain. The same legibility problem as the speed lines' dark core, solved the way a faceted world already looks.

colorDark.description: Linear RGB. The dark end of the per-mote shade range.

motes.description: The near-field air: a persistent, speed-scaled field of small faceted motes in a shell around the camera, static in the world while alive and respawning ahead once they fall behind, scaled by the player's `speedFx` comfort setting. ANNIVERSARY.md S1, the vection warning in section 2.6, and DEV-080.

randomDirection.description: DEV-272. How much of a randomDirection shape's direction is random. 1 is the port's own long-standing behaviour EXACTLY - Unity 5 serialises ShapeModule.randomDirection as a bool, the raw YAML on Checkpoint_Ring.prefab says randomDirection: 1 with no randomDirectionAmount field at all, and the port read that as 'replace the cone with a uniform sample on the sphere'. Two of the gate's three one-shot bursts are authored at 7.78 and 18.9 degrees, and a sphere is roughly 1,100x the solid angle of the first, so at 1 the same particle count arrives at about a thousandth of the density in the direction the player is looking. Below 1 the random direction is blended TOWARD the authored cone; 0 is the cone as authored. THE NUMBER TO ARGUE WITH, from the cockpit, at speed.

strength.description: Peak OVERLAY ALPHA at the outermost pixel, before the speed curve and the comfort slider. Not a luminance and not a gain: the quad composites source-over, so this is literally the fraction of the frame edge replaced by the ring's own glow on the frame the gate was crossed. THE NUMBER TO ARGUE WITH.

seconds.description: How long the pulse lasts. 0.2 is ANNIVERSARY.md S6's own figure, unargued and unmeasured. Wall clock, fed frame deltas, never the fixed step.

decayShape.description: Decay exponent on (1 - t/seconds). 1 is linear; 2 is already at a quarter of the peak by the halfway point, which is what makes a fifth of a second read as a flash with a tail rather than as a lamp held on for a fifth of a second.

innerRadius.description: UV radius where the band begins — centre 0, edge midpoint 0.5, corner 0.707. The minimum is `R_CLOSED_STRONG` from `src/render/aperture.ts`, the aperture the strongest comfort vignette is willing to black out entirely, so the pulse can only ever reach pixels the comfort layer already treats as peripheral. Research 05 R7: *chromatic/vignette pulses at the periphery only*. 0 would be the whole-frame flash S6 also asks for, and is the half R7 refuses.

feather.description: UV width of the band's soft inner edge. A hard rim is a second thing moving in the frame — the same argument `vignette.ts`'s own FEATHER is there for.

streaks.description: Wedges around the ring: a COUNT, not a frequency in hertz. Each is a radial brightening, which is what makes the band read as air going past rather than as a lamp switched on. INTEGER, and that is a correctness requirement rather than tidiness: the shader takes the angle from `atan(y, x)`, whose branch cut runs along -x, and `cos(theta * n + phase)` is continuous across that cut only when n is whole. A fractional count draws a seam down the left of the frame, in one place, for ever.

streakDepth.description: How deep the wedges cut. 0 is a smooth band with no streaks in it at all; 1 puts a dark gap between every pair.

tint.description: 0-1 blend from the ring's OWN glow colour toward white. The colour itself is NOT a key here, because it is extracted rather than tuned: `props.checkpointRing.frameGlowColor` is 2016's colour for the glow of the thing you just flew through, and DEV-069's lesson is to import the key the sheet already has rather than to type a plausible number beside it.

gainBySpeed.description: Gain against FORWARD SPEED IN M/S — the same quantity `Ship_HoverShip.ForwardSpeed` gates 2016's particles on. Deliberately the SAME breakpoints as `audio.speedCurves.gateWhooshGain`: one event, two channels, one shape, so the ear and the eye cannot disagree about how big a gate was.

gatePulse.description: The gate pass as an EVENT (ANNIVERSARY.md S6, DEV-108). 2016's one-shot ring burst and S4's whoosh already fire from the same call site in `boot/app.ts`; this is the third channel — a peripheral streak pulse riding on the comfort vignette's own draw call. Scaled by the speed FX comfort slider, like S1, S2 and S3 (section 2.6 names S6's pulse explicitly).

heightMetres.description: Metres from the ship to the VISIBLE sea (the ocean's field plus this frame's bob) at and above which there is no spray. The number to argue with. Above zero.

fullSpeed.description: m/s. The full rate from here up. Above minSpeed.

rate.description: Particles per second at the water and at fullSpeed.

carry.description: 0-1: how much of the SHIP's velocity the spray is thrown with.

angleDeg.description: Degrees either side of straight up. Below 90.

radius.description: Metres. The disc under the hull the spray is thrown from.

lifetime.description: Seconds a droplet lives, at most; each draws 60-100 % of it. Above zero.

size.description: Metres. A droplet's size, at most. Above zero.

drag.description: Per second: how fast the air slows a droplet.

colour.description: sRGB, the way the preset's other colours are picked. Anniversary's is render.coast's foamColor typed again rather than read: Classic's coast zeroes its foam, so a spray that borrowed it would be black the day somebody pins the spray on over Classic.

shade.description: Multiplies the colour: an unlit droplet against the lit sea.

waterSpray.description: DEV-429, NEXT.md P3 #2 (water first). Matt, 2026-09-26: 'plz continue the polish elements like water over the hull when going over water'. The sea throws spray at a HoverJet skimming it: nothing unless the surface under the ship is sea (the ocean's field above the island's) and the ship is within heightMetres of it and moving. Paper, not light: water does not glow. On the speed-FX comfort slider, because spray streaming past the hull is optic flow. The JumpSeat has 2016's own ground_fx and gets none.

carry.description: 0-1: how much of the HITTER's velocity the burst leaves with. The number to argue with: 0 is a puff hanging where the tree was, 1 a cloud that keeps pace with the ship.

spread.description: m/s of scatter on top of the carry, in every direction.

radius.description: Metres. The ball the burst is born in, about the contact point.

lifetime.description: Seconds a piece lives, at most; each draws 60-100 % of it. Above zero.

size.description: Metres. A piece's size, at most; each draws 60-100 % of it. Above zero.

drag.description: Per second: how fast the air takes a piece's speed away.

shade.description: Multiplies the prop's own face colours: an unlit piece against the lit tree.

colourBand.description: 0-1 of the prop's height either side of the contact: the faces whose colours the burst takes. A strike in the crown throws leaves, one at the foot throws bark.

maxMetres.description: Metres from the eye beyond which a strike throws nothing: a racer's strike far down the course is under a pixel.

propBurst.description: DEV-428: what a struck plant that stands (gameplay.propCollision.strike) throws, in the prop's own face colours, carrying some of the hitter's velocity. Paper, not light. Here and not in gameplay because every gameplay number is hashed into the lap rules (DEV-372).

emitters.description: Splashes that can be in the air at once. Past it the oldest gives way: a fixed pool, so a pod leaping together cannot add to the frame.

maxMetres.description: Metres from the eye past which a splash is not thrown.

refSpeed.description: m/s at which a crosser of body 1 throws a splash of scale 1. Scale is body x sqrt(speed / refSpeed).

maxScale.description: The biggest a splash gets: a jet going into the sea fast. A splash k times the size is k times every length, its height included, and sqrt(k) the time.

jetBody.description: A HoverJet's body, against a dolphin's.

outScale.description: x the scale of a splash coming OUT of the water against one going in.

exitMetres.description: Metres a jet that went in must rise over the visible sea to count as out: the band that keeps a skim one splash.

minSeconds.description: Seconds between two splashes by one jet, at least.

carry.description: 0-1: how much of the crosser's velocity the splash carries.

gravity.description: x the world's 32 m/s2, both parts.

drag.description: Per second: how fast the air slows a piece, both parts.

shade.description: x both parts' colour: unlit pieces against the lit sea.

count.description: Triangles in one splash of this part, and the most one splash can have alive.

lift.description: m/s up off the water at scale 1 (each draw 50-100 %).

angleDeg.description: Degrees either side of straight up. Under 90: a cone past flat throws into the sea.

radius.description: Metres: the disc it is thrown from, at scale 1. The crown is thrown from its RIM.

lifetime.description: Seconds a piece lives, at most, at scale 1 (each draws 60-100 %).

size.description: Metres. A piece's size, at most, at scale 1.

crown.description: The ring of spray, thrown up and out from the rim of a disc.

count.description: Triangles in one splash of this part, and the most one splash can have alive.

lift.description: m/s up off the water at scale 1 (each draw 50-100 %).

angleDeg.description: Degrees either side of straight up. Under 90: a cone past flat throws into the sea.

radius.description: Metres: the disc it is thrown from, at scale 1. The crown is thrown from its RIM.

lifetime.description: Seconds a piece lives, at most, at scale 1 (each draws 60-100 %).

size.description: Metres. A piece's size, at most, at scale 1.

drops.description: The droplets, a narrower, faster cone from the middle.

splash.description: DEV-613: a splash where anything goes into the sea or comes out of it: a dolphin leaving it and landing, a HoverJet (the player's or a racer's) whose hull meets it and rises back out. Paper, not light. A look (D35): 2016 threw none.

vapourCone.description: DEV-926: a ring of mist riding the ship near top speed. edition-schema.ts EditionVapourCone has each field.

boostShockwave.description: DEV-927: a ring of air thrown out where boost engages. edition-schema.ts EditionBoostShockwave has each field.

wingVortices.description: DEV-928: wing-tip vortices in a hard turn. edition-schema.ts EditionWingVortices has each field.

emissive.description: A floor under the cockpit material so the deepest faces never reach true black. It is UNIFORM over the mesh, so it flattens — keep it well below what the two lights do or it undoes them. Zero means the material is not touched at all, which is what Classic wants.

lighting.description: The cabin lighting pass: a dim fill high and behind the eye that rakes the canopy frame from inside, a glow under the readout, and an emissive floor. The struts render near-black because their own `COLOR_0` is 0.1559, the shipped material tint was missing (fixed for BOTH presets — `render/lambert1.ts`), and indoors the only diffuse light in the game is the Skyshop probe at 0.5974 while the sun is 4 degrees above the horizon and rakes the OUTSIDE. ANNIVERSARY.md V8, DEV-088.

hands.description: Draw the arms, the hands and the two controls they hold. A second escape hatch on the part of a procedural body that goes wrong first: the seat and the legs stand on their own without it.

palette.description: Four colours, flat-shaded, in the game's own idiom. The stand-in has no textures and never will.

body.description: A body in the seat. 2016 rendered `pilot_scifi_rigged` (Mixamo) and `MM_Commander_Chair_01`, and research 05 counts a rendered pilot body in its comfort inventory — but neither asset can ship (CLAUDE.md rule 7), so `render/cockpit-body.ts` builds a first-party stand-in from the MEASURED seat offsets: the chair's mesh origin and the pilot's land 1.322 and 1.323 m below the eye, which is the cockpit floor. Optional, because a body that is wrong is worse than none. ANNIVERSARY.md V8, DEV-088.

tilt.description: RADIANS about the ship's x axis. Negative tips the top of the panel away from the eye, toward the console face it sits in.

scale.description: Uniform scale on the panel: 2016's two screens in the dash (the upper one 0.351 x 0.156 m). 1 is 2016's size.

hud.description: Where the HoverJet's readout sits, from its `EYE`: the pose of 2016's upper screen, `Ship_HUD/panel_shipUI` composed out of `PlayerShip_SR14_Photon.prefab`, which sets it into the dash's recess 14-36 mm proud of the near-black glass (DEV-362, `render/hud-dash.ts`). This used to cite '46 dark console vertices, centroid (0, 0.432, 0.94)' — the console's back between the pilot's knees, not the screen.

tilt.description: RADIANS about the ship's x axis. Negative tips the top of the panel away from the eye.

scale.description: Uniform scale on the JumpSeat's panel.

jumpSeatHud.description: Where the JumpSeat's readout sits, from its `JUMPSEAT_EYE`. It shared `hud` until DEV-362 set the HoverJet's into its dash; 2016's JumpSeat gauge stood free in front of the shell, so this keeps the pose both vehicles had.

placement.description: Where the cockpit-mounted elements sit. NOT a feature — there is no off — so it is not in `editionFeatures` and both presets carry the same numbers; the block exists so `?lookdev=1`'s Placement folder edits a value the build reads and its Copy JSON pastes here. The cabin lamps and the pilot already carry their own `offset` under `cockpit.lighting` and `cockpit.body`, and the panel reaches those too. DEV-129.

startSpeed.description: Metres per second. Below it there is no buffet AND no slope, because the ramp is squared — so crossing this speed fades in rather than popping on. Never below `hoverjet.ship.minEffectsSpeed` (25), the speed at which the shipped game itself starts drawing air.

fullSpeed.description: Metres per second at which the speed ramp reaches 1 and stops growing; above it the per-stage gain carries the effect. Must exceed `startSpeed` — `validateEdition` refuses otherwise, because the difference is a divisor.
