amplitude.description: METRES: peak translation of `art_pivot` at ramp 1, stage gain 1, comfort slider full. A ceiling, not a typical value — the waveform is the MEAN of `frequency`'s sines, so the RMS excursion is about 0.41 of this.

angle.description: RADIANS: peak roll and pitch of `art_pivot`, same conditions as `amplitude`. It is a buffet, not an earthquake: a fraction of a degree at cruise.

stageGain.description: Multiplier per boost stage, indexed 0..3 against `hoverjet.ship.minBoostEffectsSpeed` / `_stage2_speed` / `_stage3_speed`. The shake steps where the boost plume steps because they are the same event.

frequency.description: HERTZ. One sine per entry per channel, phases spread by the golden angle. Keep every entry well under half the display rate (72 Hz in a headset) or the buffet reads as a strobe rather than as air.

fullThrottle.description: AMPLITUDE multiplier on the buffet with the engine at its full-throttle thrust, unboosted — and below it, where the speed the buffet is keyed on already falls.

boost.description: AMPLITUDE multiplier the instant a boost spools up from the unboosted terminal. Blended from `fullThrottle` by the SPOOLED thrust, not the button, so it never pops.

topSpeed.description: AMPLITUDE multiplier boosting at 'top speed', the speed chain's LIVE boosted terminal (180 m/s at no chain, ~335 at twenty-one gates). Faded from `boost` linearly in speed from the live unboosted terminal to that one.

throttle.description: DEV-426: the buffet follows the ENGINE as well as the speed. Matt, 2026-09-26: *"0.6x the current jitter at full throttle and then 1x the jitter at boost, and then fade back to 0.8x jitter once at top speed. (multiplier is amplitude, not speed)"*. Optional: absent is 1 everywhere, the buffet before DEV-426. HoverJet only; the JumpSeat has no boost and no chain. `game/cockpit-shake.ts`'s `throttleShakeGain` is the curve.

shake.description: Cockpit shake, never camera shake: the cockpit MESH vibrates with speed and boost stage around a still rig. ANNIVERSARY.md S3, and the Squadrons rule in section 2.4. It is a speed effect, so it ALSO scales by the `speedFx` comfort slider and is zero when that is off (section 2.6).

engine.description: The engine's own voice, beyond S4: a sub-octave rumble under the 2016 loops, and a pitch that follows FORWARD SPEED (S4's follows the throttle). Two flags because they are two sounds and Matt may want one without the other. 2016 has zero runtime pitch modulation, so both are off on Classic and carry no-op numbers there. DEV-137.

gainByThrottle.description: Throttle 0..1 -> gain multiplier on `engine.rumble`, the Thrusters loop's own tonal layers an octave down plus a sub sine, low-passed. Non-zero at zero throttle so the bed has weight at idle; rises with the stick.

cutoffHz.description: Low-pass cutoff in Hz on the rumble voice while the burner is out. Sets how much of the octave-down sawtooths' harmonics survive: around 180 Hz keeps the 47 / 94 / 141 Hz partials and takes the noise's top off.

boostGain.description: Multiplies the rumble gain while the afterburner is lit. 1 is no change.

boostCutoffHz.description: The rumble's low-pass cutoff while the afterburner is lit. Opening it is what lets the sawtooth harmonics through, which is most of the growl.

growlGain.description: Gain multiplier on `engine.growl`, the second sub layer that runs only while the burner is lit: the AfterBurner loop an octave down plus a partner tone a fifth above it, whose difference tone is the 29 Hz roughness a growl is. 0 is no growl layer at all.

rumble.description: A deep rumble under the 2016 engine loops. The 2016 loops are unchanged and still on top; this is a low-passed copy of the thruster an octave down, mixed under them, so Classic's character survives with weight added. DEV-137.

rateBySpeed.description: Forward speed m/s -> playback-rate multiplier on EVERY engine loop (idle, thrusters, afterburner, rumble, growl) and on the AI racers' engines. 1 is as authored. Multiplies S4's throttle rate rather than replacing it: the stick answers fast, the air answers slow. The Anniversary knees sit on the sheet's four 2016 speed gates (25 / 120 / 240 / 350) so idle, cruise and boost land where 2016's loop swaps sat — `tests/unit/audio-engine-sound.test.ts` asserts that against the generated constants.

slewPerSecond.description: The most the tracked rate may move in one second, in rate units. A crash puts the speed to zero in one tick; without this the engine would chirp down an octave-fraction in 12 ms. 0.25 walks a stall down over about a second and never limits ordinary acceleration (which moves the rate ~0.02 a second).

pitchTracking.description: Engine pitch that tracks forward speed. 2016 swaps loops at fixed pitch and never modulates one; S4 (DEV-084) put the throttle on the thruster's rate; this puts the AIR on every engine voice. DEV-137.

aircraftWindGain.description: Airspeed m/s -> gain 0..1 on `AircraftWind`, 2016's low roar above `minEffectsSpeed` (25). Starts at zero AT the threshold so the layer fades up out of nothing instead of snapping on, and rolls back as `FlightWind` takes over — that crossfade is what replaces 2016's 0.15 s duck at 120.

flightWindGain.description: Airspeed m/s -> gain 0..1 on `FlightWind`, the bright rush 2016 fires once on entering the 120..240 band and then never stops. On this preset the curve stops it, so `windLoopsNeverStop` is off.

windCutoffHz.description: Airspeed m/s -> low-pass cutoff in Hz, on BOTH wind loops. One curve because it stands for one quantity: how much air is going past the canopy. The top value should be transparent (12 kHz+), not a filter you can hear sitting there.

thrustRate.description: Throttle 0..1 -> playback rate on the thruster loop, as a frequency multiplier (the same meaning `CueSpec.pitch` carries — see `src/audio/cues.ts`). 1 is as authored. 2016 modulates NOTHING at runtime; this is the deviation.

afterburnerRate.description: Throttle 0..1 -> playback rate on the afterburner loop.

afterburnerStep.description: Rate multiplier applied to the THRUSTER while the burner is lit — the jump a pilot hears when the boost comes in. 1 is no step. On the thruster rather than the burner because `Input_Ship.cs:426` needs both triggers, so the burner never sounds alone.

gateWhooshGain.description: Airspeed m/s at the pass -> gain multiplier 0..1 on the gate whoosh. Zero everywhere is the no-op.

gateWhooshPitch.description: Airspeed m/s at the pass -> pitch multiplier on the gate whoosh. Faster is higher, which is what a faster pass sounds like; `src/audio/speed-curves.ts` says why it is pitch rather than length.

windRate.description: Airspeed m/s -> playback-rate multiplier on BOTH wind loops, the same meaning `CueSpec.pitch` carries: every noise layer's filter band and the flight wind's tone move by it, so the air rises in pitch as well as brightening and swelling. 1 is as authored. Matt, 2026-09-26: *"would love if engine noise and wind sounds changed/pitch-shifted as i moved faster"*. 2016 has no runtime pitch; Classic carries a flat 1. DEV-425.

speedCurves.description: Wind gain and low-pass as curves of airspeed, engine pitch with throttle, a whoosh on a gate pass. 2016 had none of it — zero runtime pitch modulation in first-party code — so Classic keeps the loop swaps at fixed pitch and carries no-op curves here. ANNIVERSARY.md S4, DEV-084.

rateBySpeed.description: Platform speed m/s -> playback-rate multiplier on `elevator.motor`, the same meaning `CueSpec.pitch` carries. The speed is the lift's own, derived tick to tick from the ride curve (`launch.rise`), so the motor spins up, cruises and spins down with whatever curve the level carries. int_01's peaks near 15 m/s.

gainBySpeed.description: Platform speed m/s -> gain multiplier 0..1 on `elevator.motor`. Zero at rest, so the voice rises out of nothing as the platform starts and falls back into it as it stops.

stoppedBelow.description: Platform speed m/s under which the lift counts as stopped. The motor starts when the platform first rises above it and stops, with the arrival clunk, when it falls back below it.

arriveGain.description: Gain multiplier on `elevator.arrive`, the clunk as the platform locks at the top. 0 is none.

lift.description: The lift ride's motor and its arrival. 2016's ride is a servo at the press, a loop that ships MUTED and eight positional whooshes (AUD-1 plays the loop on both editions); nothing in it follows the platform. Matt, 2026-09-26: *"need sound fx for the elevator ride"*. Classic carries no-op numbers. DEV-424.

subdivisionByLod.description: Sub-quads per edge of every ocean facet, INDEXED BY LOD; the last entry covers every level beyond it. 1 is the mesh the generator produced and is 2016 exactly; 8 splits each facet into 64 and is what the port has drawn at every distance since DEV-023 (Matt: 'the ocean isn't nearly dense enough ... roughly 4x denser', measured at 8). The ladder spends facets where one is more than a few pixels across and stops spending them where it is not. What that saves is UNMEASURED: the only reading of the sea's vertex cost (`?ocean=8` -> `?ocean=1`) is withdrawn (`docs/plan/VR-PERF-WAVE-2-WORK.md` §6b), and on `int_01` the ladder is inert over most of the route, where every built sea chunk is at LOD 0 (DEV-183 §3 — a triangle count, not a millisecond). Anniversary keeps 8 in the band under the ship and lets it fall to 1 by LOD 3; Classic holds 8 everywhere, which is the pre-DEV-183 build. Note that the GEOMETRY coarsens on its own as well: a LOD n chunk is a stride of 2^n over the same vertex grid, so the world-metre facet at LOD n is `baseResolution * 2^n * scale / subdivisionByLod[n]` — which is the number `render/water.ts` needs as `uFacet` and, before DEV-183, never got. `?ocean=<n>` overrides the whole ladder with one number.

ocean.description: How finely the SEA is drawn, band by band. DEV-183. Not a feature with an `enabled`: every preset draws the ocean at some density, and Classic's is a ladder like any other.

diagonalFix.description: DEV-831. On: each terrain quad is split along the diagonal 2016's code meant to pick (the one that better fits the height map). Off: the diagonal its bug picks (the midpoint's HEIGHT used as its depth), which is what 2016 shipped and Classic keeps. Read when a world is built, so a mid-flight look swap takes effect on the next world.

durationScale.description: Multiplies the sheet's authored `lodTransitionTime` for each terrain (1 s on Simonet's islands, 0.6 s on its ocean, 1 s alpine, 0.6 desert) to give the length of the screen-door cross-fade between two LODs. 1 is exactly what 2016 wrote down per environment and never rendered (its alpha material was opaque — DEV-130). 0 is a hard swap even with the flag on. Above about 2 the fade is slower than the ship crosses a chunk, and two transitions of one chunk can overlap only in the sense that the second waits for the first (`load-terrain.ts` never re-requests a fading chunk).

lodFade.description: The LOD cross-fade 2016 authored and never got. Both meshes drawn for the transition, each fragment owned by exactly one of them (interleaved-gradient dither), no blending and no depth fight. DEV-130, `render/lod-fade.ts`.

rung.description: DEV-237. How much of the land's shading the bake replaces, and it is a PICTURE rather than a coefficient: it selects which `#define` the terrain's base material carries and therefore which program three compiles. 3 drops everything -- the physical chain, both PMREM fetches, the GGX lobe, the five-tap PCF and `ff2SunHeightTerm` all sit behind a dead `totalDiffuse` and the compiler removes them -- and is the rung DEV-232 measured at -0.80 ms p50 / -1.15 p95 on `adv_02_jumpSeat`. It costs the ground its shadows: the ship, the racers and the landmarks stop casting onto it, which ANNIVERSARY.md ranks second of the eight scale cues. 1 keeps the shadow multiply per fragment (`outgoingLight = diffuseColor.rgb * ff2ShadowOnly()`, so `getShadow` and `ff2SunHeightTerm` both still run) and buys less. Its millisecond is unmeasured; its picture is not, and it is NOT the faithful rung the plan called it: three multiplies a shadow into `directLight.color` only, so a shadowed hillside still receives the light probe's irradiance, while a bake that has collapsed direct and indirect into one vertex colour shadows the ambient with it. Photographed on `adv_02_jumpSeat`: rung 3 sits 2.07 mean levels of 255 from the shipped build, rung 1 sits 33.9 levels darker. DEV-237. There is NO rung 2: the plan's rung 2 bakes `ff2SunHeightTerm` as well, which puts the static shadow terminator back on the 8 m grid that `render/far-shadow.ts`'s signed field exists to get it off, so it is a separate argument and is not built. 3 is the value that reproduces the shipped build byte for byte. `split` is DEV-240, and it is the correction DEV-237 costed and refused to guess at: the bake stops collapsing the two halves of the diffuse, the ambient stays in the `color` attribute, the sun N.L term goes into a second vec3 attribute `ff2Direct`, and the shader writes `ambient + direct * ff2ShadowOnly()`. That is three own semantics term for term -- `lights_fragment_begin` multiplies the shadow into `directLight.color` and `getLightProbeIrradiance` never sees one -- so the ground keeps every cast shadow rung 1 keeps while sitting where rung 3 sits against the shipped picture. It costs 12 bytes a vertex and one varying; `__ff2.bakedLight().directBytes` is the measured figure on the environment in front of you. There is NO rung named 2 and no rung numbered 4: the name is a name on purpose, because the plan ladder is numbered and a fourth integer would read as a position on it.

bakedLight.description: DEV-232. Compute the LAND's diffuse lighting once, into its vertex colours, and gate three's physical chain out behind it. It is exact rather than approximate here: `sim/terrain/faceted.ts` writes one normal and one colour to all three vertices of every triangle, `render/skyshop-ibl.ts` forces `iblIrradiance` to zero so the whole indirect diffuse is a light probe's spherical harmonics, and DEV-192 already cut the point-light loop -- so every diffuse term is a function of the face normal and storing it per vertex loses nothing. What it DOES lose is the view-dependent half: the environment reflection, the GGX lobe, `terrain.surfaceGloss` (DEV-132) with them, and both shadow terms, so the ship and the landmarks stop casting onto the ground. No numbers here because it has none -- the sun and the probe are read off the scene. Off in both editions until it is measured and Matt has seen it; see docs/plan/DEV-232-BAKED-LIGHT.md. The one knob is `rung` (DEV-237), and it is not a tuning number -- it picks a picture. Off in both editions until a rung is chosen and Matt has seen it.

roughness.description: GGX roughness for every facet whose vertex colour is nearest one of this class's swatches. For scale: the sea's own value, transcribed from its VacuumShaders _Shininess, is 0.27; the whole island on Classic is 0.17. Matt's order is water < grass < rock, and `terrain-surface.test.ts` holds it against the sheet.

swatches.description: Colour-map values 0..1 as STORED — the sRGB bytes `FacetedTerrain` stamps on the facet, before the material tint, which is exactly what the vertex colour carries into the shader. Measured by k-means over the imported maps (DEV-132); the same six appear on Simonet, alpine and Kauai. Sixteen swatches in total across all classes is the shader's table.

classes.description: Nearest-swatch classification, so a class may hold several swatches (the desert's red/brown rock beside Simonet's pale rock). An empty list is the identity.

surfaceGloss.description: Per-facet roughness from the facet's own colour class. DEV-132, `render/terrain-surface.ts`. Only `roughnessFactor` moves; F0, tint and vertex colour stay DEV-008's and DEV-014's.

smoothMetres.description: METRES of reconstruction between the height map's 8-bit levels, applied to the RING'S grid only (DEV-131). One level is terrainHeight / 255 — 6.02 m on Simonet, 4.02 m elsewhere — and the 4 m grid samples texel centres exactly, so without this every riser is a whole level and every shelf is flat: terraces. The reconstruction is a triangle blur of this radius clamped to within half a level of the stored map, so nothing it produces contradicts the data and a genuine cliff keeps its height to within 3 m. Twelve texels (48 m) covers the p90 shelf on Simonet's 4 m grid (36 m). 0 samples the base map exactly, which is what LOD 0 and Classic do.

baseResolution.description: METRES per quad inside the ring, against the 8 m the whole world is drawn at. Must be a POWER OF TWO and finer than the terrain's own `baseResolution` — it has to divide `chunkSize` exactly or the chunk would not reach its own edge, and every shipped chunk is 256, 512 or 1024 m. 4 is one rung: four times the interior triangles of the same chunk at 8. 2 is sixteen times, and is not a default — on Simonet it is 33,800 triangles a chunk against 2,312, and its vertex grid is 2049 squared (50 MB) against 1025 squared (12.6 MB). `validateEdition` checks the power of two; `sim/terrain/detail.ts` throws with the real chunk size.

radius.description: METRES, HORIZONTAL, to the chunk FOOTPRINT — the same measure every LOD band uses, so altitude never pushes the ground under the ship out of the ring (`deltaToChunk.y = 0`, and that is 2016's rule). Zero is the no-op: `detailBand` returns null and LOD -1 becomes unreachable. Keep it well inside the terrain's own `lodDistance` (700 m on alpine, 800 on desert, 1024 on Simonet and Kauai) so the ring never argues with the coarsening ladder. Budget scales with the square: on Simonet's 256 m chunks, 320 m is at most 14 chunks and 512 m is 24.

jitterScale.description: Multiplies the TERRAIN'S OWN `randomOffset` on the finer grid — a ratio, not a length, so one number is right for every environment (Simonet jitters 1.3 m, desert and alpine 0.8, Kauai 1.3). 2016 tuned those against an 8 m facet, which is 10-16 % of the pitch; carried unchanged onto a 4 m grid they become 20-33 %, and two neighbours moving 1.3 m each way on a 4 m pitch is noise that folds triangles rather than crumpled rock. 0.5 with a halved resolution keeps the ratio exactly, so the finer grain reads as the same rock, smaller — which is the fractal-spectrum argument in ANNIVERSARY.md section 1.4, not a new look.

maxInFlight.description: How many detail chunks may be awaiting a worker reply at once. The worker is serial, so this does not change throughput — it changes STALENESS: a ship crossing the island at 180 m/s sweeps the ring onto a new column of chunks every 1.4 s, and without a cap one frame enqueues everything that just came into range while the LOD 1 to 0 regenerations the player can actually see queue behind it. A shallow queue re-decides from the current camera position every few chunks. LOD 0 and above are never routed through the cap.

detailRing.description: LOD -1: the chunks within `radius` of the ship generated at a finer facet, in the worker, on demand. 2016 has ONE grain size at every distance (8 m) and a LOD ladder that only ever goes coarser, which ANNIVERSARY.md section 1.4 diagnoses as the miniature tell — with no shadow, no haze and no human-scale object, the eye assumes the facets are ordinary ground clutter and a 35 m gate reads as a 4 m one. Section 2.1 says the same from the speed side: 11 facet edges a second at 90 m/s and 300 m up. Same chunk boundaries, same skirts, same diagonal bug, same colour sampling — it is `generateChunk` at a different pitch, not a second generator. The COLLISION height field is untouched (DEV-041). ANNIVERSARY.md T1, DEV-085.

cells.description: Cells per side of every level's window; EVEN, because each window is snapped to its coarser neighbour's lattice. 64 with innerCell 32 gives the four levels +-1,024 / 2,048 / 4,096 / 8,192 m.

innerCell.description: The finest level's cell, WORLD metres. Must divide the plate's parent quad (256 m on both ocean plates) a whole number of times: 32 is Matt's DEV-023 density (every parent triangle split 8 x 8). Each level doubles it.

faceNormals.description: DEV-340. The sea's face normal from the ring VERTEX shader (each vertex displaces all three corners of its triangle and passes the unit normal as a flat varying) instead of the fragment's dFdx/dFdy. One exact normal per face, no derivative, nothing at facet edges where a 2x2 pixel quad straddles two faces. Off until measured and seen.

levels.description: How many levels. Level k is the plate's LOD k at the same split, so its vertices are the plate's own (`tests/unit/ocean-ring-lattice.test.ts`).

oceanRings.description: DEV-339, docs/plan/OCEAN-PERF.md. The sea as camera-centred rings (a geometry clipmap) instead of the plate's 8 km chunks: facet size is a function of distance from the eye, one mesh built once, no LOD swaps, no fades. A look flag: the collision surface is the height field, never a mesh. `render/ocean-rings.ts`.

terrain.description: The terrain generator's presentation knobs. The generator itself, its bugs and its collision surface are the ledger's and are not reachable from here.

menu.description: The level select's room and tables. Render only.

holoTerrainColours.description: The holotable island drawn as a PROJECTION of the terrain's own colours (DEV-140). The colours are not the flag: 2016's art_levelSel_* miniatures were full-colour vertex-painted terrain (Faceted Terrain_miniMaps.mat, Marmoset/Vertex Color/Specular IBL, _Color 0.941, emission black), so both presets draw the palette cut from the environment's colour map (content/palettes/, tools/extract/palette.mjs). What `enabled` switches on is the port's TELL that the island is a hologram rather than a model: a brightness lift, a lean toward the room's holo tint, a rim where facets turn away, faint scanlines. Off, the island is 2016's plain miniature.

brightness.description: Multiplier on the island's colour. 1 is the colour map's own byte on screen, shaded by the relief light baked into the faces (DEV-579); it was the byte read raw as linear until then, which drew chalk.

holoMix.description: 0..1 lean of every face toward the holo tint (the HUD accent family). The hue tell; 0 is the terrain's colour untouched.

rim.description: Strength of the grazing-angle rim, in the holo tint. The silhouette tell; 0 is none.

scanline.description: 0..1 depth of the horizontal scanline darkening across the model. The projection tell; 0 is none.

medalOutline.description: A dark silhouette shell behind the medal, so a pale tier reads against a pale island (DEV-151). DEV-140 gave the islands the terrain's own colours in both presets, and 2016's medal is the title emblem in the tier's own _Color (DEV-113), pale on four tiers of five; measured over all four palettes, every tier but bronze sits under WCAG's 3:1 for a graphical object across most of every island, and over Simonet's white rock bronze fails too. The tier colours are 2016's and may not move, so the readability comes from the SHAPE: an inverted hull a little larger than the emblem, drawn back-faces-only, which is a dark border round the outline from every angle and for every tier. Anniversary only — 2016 had the same problem and shipped it, so this is curation, not a bug fix.

widthFraction.description: How far the shell stands off the emblem, as a fraction of the emblem's own HEIGHT — not metres, because the emblem is scaled to the table and a fixed offset would be a hairline on one and a blob on another. A point r from the emblem's centre moves out by 2*widthFraction*r, so the band at the top and bottom edges is exactly widthFraction times the height.

colour.description: The shell's colour, sRGB 0..1. Dark: it is a border, not a glow, and it is what makes the medal read against a bright island. Near-black rather than black so it sits in the hangar's own darkest tone.

opacity.description: 0..1 opacity of the shell. 1 is a solid border.

gameplay.description: THE ONLY BLOCK THAT CHANGES THE GAME. Section 0.2: anything that changes scoring, rules or routes is a separate, explicitly gameplay-tagged flag, and Classic never reads it. Everything else in this file is presentation, and a Classic run and an Anniversary run of the same flight score the same; under this block they do not. ANNIVERSARY.md section 4.1, DEV-110.

nearMetres.description: METRES of ground clearance at or below which the meter reads FULL. Must be below `farMetres` - inverted, the meter reads full at altitude and empty on the deck, which is a lever rewarding the exact opposite of what it is for, with nothing about the frame looking wrong. `edition-schema.ts` refuses it.

farMetres.description: METRES at or above which the meter reads nothing. Linear between the two, deliberately: this is a scoring signal a player has to be able to predict, and an ease is not learnable.

maxBonus.description: The bonus at a full meter as a FRACTION of the gate's own points - 1 doubles a gate taken on the deck. NOT a multiplier on 2016's scorers: the points go into a separate pool, which keeps the shipped scorers byte-exact and lets the results panel say "4,200 + 900" rather than "5,100". 0 is exactly the shipped score, which makes this the clean A/B dial. THE NUMBER TO ARGUE WITH, and the section 5 table says it is settled by playtest rather than by measurement.

minSpeed.description: METRES PER SECOND below which nothing accrues however low you are. The anti-hover clause: without it the optimal play is to stop dead one metre off a hillside, which is the opposite of what the lever is for - it rewards the low LINE, and a line has a speed.

attackSeconds.description: Seconds for the meter to rise. Short - the reward should feel immediate.

releaseSeconds.description: Seconds for it to fall, LONGER than the attack. A meter that empties the instant you clear a ridge punishes the terrain for having a far side, and it flickers on every crest - which is a second thing moving in the periphery, the same argument the comfort vignette makes about its own asymmetry.

perSecond.description: POINTS PER SECOND banked at a FULL meter, pro rata at a partial one, on EVERY mission (DEV-154). 0 is the DEV-110 behaviour - the gate channel and nothing else - so this is the second clean A/B dial on this block. It exists because `maxBonus` pays only AT a gate, 21 instants in an 8,174-tick lap of int_01, and the gates are not low: their centres sit 17.8 to 336.5 m above the surface, median 87.6, and NOT ONE of the twenty-one is within `nearMetres`, so a full meter at a gate is unreachable by construction and the whole gate channel caps at a quarter of what maxBonus advertises. Measured, not assumed. THE NUMBER TO ARGUE WITH, and like maxBonus it is settled by playtest.

awardStep.description: POINTS of accrual per LOW announcement. DISPLAY ONLY - it changes no score; the pool accrues every tick whatever this says, and 0 simply never announces. A rate is a state display and a player learns from events, so the accrual is chunked into `LOW +N` banners on the event row - and the CADENCE of those banners is itself the meter: pinned on the deck they arrive every awardStep/perSecond seconds, at a quarter meter four times slower.

cleanCentredness.description: 0..1, where 1 is the mathematical centre of the gate and 0 is the rim. At or above this AND at or above `minSpeed`, a gate is CLEAN. Measured on the SWEPT SEGMENT rather than at the crossing tick, and normalised by the gate's OWN trigger radius so a course with tighter rings asks for more without anything being re-tuned.

minSpeed.description: METRES PER SECOND - the "at speed" half of "through its centre at speed".

nearMissMetres.description: METRES to the NEAREST surface below which a tick counts as a near miss - since DEV-112 that is sim/surface-proximity.ts's fan of six probes plus the belly, so a canyon wall off the wingtip counts the way a ridge under the hull does. Reuses G1's reading rather than measuring anything of its own, so the two levers cannot disagree about how close the ground is. Only ever reported on a tick that did NOT strike: a near miss is by definition a miss, and (DEV-112) only at or above `minSpeed`, because points now ride on it.

nearMissCooldown.description: Seconds before another near miss may fire. A long low pass down a valley is ONE piece of flying and not four hundred events.

nearMissPoints.description: POINTS a near miss banks into G1's bonus pool (DEV-112) - the Anniversary score, never the medal: state.score never sees the pool, so the medal for a flight is identical with this on and off. 0 on Classic. Gate-independent, which is what the six missions that score no rings get from the pool. Negative is refused: a lever that can punish is a different design than the one section 4.1 argues for.

chainMeter.description: Draw the speed chain. Section 4.1: `maxSpeed += 18` per gate reverting after 5.5 s is the core skill loop and today it is invisible except as a number. NO NUMBERS OF ITS OWN on purpose - it draws what `sim/speed-chain.ts` already holds, so it cannot disagree with the mechanic it reports. It changes no score; it is in this block because a player who can see the chain plays differently, which is a change to the game even when the arithmetic is untouched.

markLength.description: A mark's length along its own radius, as a FRACTION of the clean radius. A fraction rather than metres so a course with tighter rings gets a proportionally tighter reticle with nothing re-tuned.

markThickness.description: A mark's cross-section, as a fraction of the clean radius.

pipSize.description: The centre pip's side, as a fraction of the clean radius. 0 draws no pip - the instance is still allocated and is a zero-scale box, which draws nothing.

emissive.description: Emissive intensity. The gate's 18 studs sit at 2, which is `glowyMaterial`'s own _GlowStrength off the sheet; this is the reticle's, beside them.

gateBullseye.description: DEV-153. Matt, 2026-09-16: “makes me [want] 'bullseye target' art inside the gates to show players where to aim.” 2016 drew NOTHING in the aperture - Checkpoint_Ring.prefab is 34 GameObjects and all 19 of its MeshRenderers are on the rim (jumpGate_diamond plus 18 built-in cubes under highlightCubes, at |x| 9.1-9.6 or |y| 14.3-15.5 in prefab space); the only object at the centre is ringIdle, a ParticleSystem with EmissionModule.enabled 0 and maxNumParticles 1, and TriggerCheckpoint's own checkpointArt field is null on this prefab. So Classic draws the bare frame and this is Anniversary only. THE RADIUS IS NOT A NUMBER ANYBODY PICKED: it is gateEvents.cleanCentredness against the gate's own trigger radius - `trigger.radius x (1 - cleanCentredness)`, 9.05 m on int_01's 22.62 m triggers - so the art draws the rule G2 already scores, the way chainMeter draws the chain the sim already holds. Zeroed twice over like the rest of this block: Classic's cleanCentredness is 1, which makes the radius 0 whatever the flag says. Four bars and a pip rather than a disc or a thin ring: you fly THROUGH a gate so a filled disc is a wall, a thin torus is the shape that aliases away first at the distance you commit to a line from (DEV-044), and a gate is already made of 18 bars so four more in the same material cannot read as a foreign object. It is in the gameplay block because a player who can see where CLEAN is flies differently.

usePads.description: Start one racer on every `startGrid` pad tagged `ai` - the two positions 2016 authored for its opposition - before any slot below is used. False leaves the 2016 pads empty and the grid is the slots alone.

slots.description: Extra starting positions, in the PLAYER'S frame at the release point: metres AHEAD along the spawn heading and metres to the player's RIGHT, both at the release altitude, facing the spawn heading. The grid is the pads first (when `usePads`), then these in order; the racer count is the sum. With `enabled` false the list is not read and the grid is 2016's pads. `sim/ai-racer.ts` assigns a tuning per slot unless `tuning` names one.

ahead.description: Metres ahead of the player's release point along the spawn heading. Negative is behind.

right.description: Metres to the player's right. Negative is left.

tuning.description: A key of `AI_RACER_TUNINGS`. Optional; the loader assigns the next unused tuning when absent.

laneSpacing.description: METRES between neighbouring lanes. Lanes are ranked by where each racer stood across the line and spaced evenly about it, so n racers span (n - 1) x this.

laneEaseMetres.description: METRES of arc after gate 0 over which a racer moves from where its grid slot stood it to its lane (a smoothstep). 0 takes the lane at once.

gateFraction.description: How much of a ring's trigger RADIUS the lanes, plus half a hull's beam, may use AT the ring. Every lane narrows together, keeping the pack's order, when the widest would not fit.

gateFunnel.description: METRES of lateral room regained per METRE of arc away from a ring: the funnel's slope. Shallow on purpose - a lane that narrows sharply at every ring forces the controller at its own period (the rings are ~2.9 s apart at racing speed).

avoidReach.description: METRES along the course, ahead or behind, inside which another craft (racer or player) is steered away from.

avoidClearance.description: METRES off a racer's own track, across or above, inside which another craft is steered away from. A lane apart is not avoided at all.

avoidGain.description: METRES the lane moves at full avoidance weight. The summed weight is bounded at one either way.

separation.description: DEV-364. Matt, 2026-09-24: 'our ai racers tend to converge on the same path - can you have them avoid each other.' TRUE: each racer flies its own lane off the racing line, from its grid slot, narrowing into the rings, and steers off any craft close along and across its track. FALSE: the one line every racer flew before, which is what 2016's recordings amount to. Its own feature, not composed with `gameplay.racers.enabled` (that is the grid).

restitution.description: How much of the CLOSING SPEED along the contact normal comes back out as a push. 0: the two move off together. 1: they swap it. Momentum is conserved at every value.

restingSpeed.description: METRES PER SECOND of closing speed under which a contact does not bounce at all: two ships steered gently together lean on each other rather than chattering.

passes.description: Sweeps over every pair per fixed step. One resolves a pair; more settle three in a pile.

contact.description: DEV-364. Matt, 2026-09-24: 'players can fly straight into them and through them.' TRUE: every racer and the player is a capsule off the HoverJet's own collider hull, and two that touch are pushed apart, sharing the closing speed by inverse mass - never a crash. FALSE: 2016's ghosts, which nothing could touch.

minSpeed.description: METRES PER SECOND of closing speed along the contact normal at and under which a contact is a lean, not a hit: no nudge, no sound, no jolt.

fullSpeed.description: METRES PER SECOND of closing speed at which a hit is at full strength. Strength runs linearly from 0 at `minSpeed` to 1 here, and stays 1 above. Must exceed `minSpeed`.

scrub.description: The fraction of the PLAYER'S speed a full-strength hit takes away, on top of what the push shares.

headingKick.description: RADIANS PER SECOND of angular velocity swinging the nose toward the direction the push threw the ship, at full strength. The body's own angular drag bleeds it away.

attitudeKick.description: RADIANS PER SECOND of angular velocity tipping the canopy toward the push, at full strength: a hit from the left lifts the left wing, a rear-end dips the nose.

shakeSeconds.description: SECONDS, render time, the cockpit's jolt takes to die away. The jolt is `cockpit.shake`'s own waveform, so it follows that feature's flag and the speed-effects slider.

shakeGain.description: The jolt's peak at full strength, in multiples of `cockpit.shake.amplitude` and `cockpit.shake.angle`, added to the buffet.

hit.description: DEV-364 follow-up. Matt, 2026-09-25: 'sound and physics cost - nudge the players as if they got hit.' TRUE: when a racer strikes the PLAYER harder than `minSpeed`, the player's speed is scrubbed and its nose and canopy knocked toward the push (in the sim, deterministic), 2016's configured-and-never-called `hit` cue plays, and the cockpit jolts. A racer takes the push alone. Composed with `contact`: nothing touches, nothing is hit. FALSE: DEV-364's push and nothing else.

racers.description: How many AI racers stand on the grid and where. DEV-125 (Matt, 2026-09-16: 'add 3 more racers to the hover jet. these should be aligned in front of the player at the race start'). Changes the RACE and therefore the results panel, which is why it is in this block. The racers' flight model, autopilot and finish rule are untouched.

minImpactSpeed.description: METRES PER SECOND of velocity INTO the surface (the normal component, the part the zero-bounciness contact removes) at or above which a contact is a crash rather than a scrape. Below it the ship bounces off exactly as 2016's did.

resetBackMetres.description: METRES of arc length BEHIND the crash, along the course line, at which the ship is put back. 'Near the crash but back on the course' - far enough that the same hillside is not the first thing ahead.

clearanceMetres.description: METRES above the collision surface the reset point is lifted to when the course line itself is lower than that. The authored line is certified clear (min AGL 18 m); the gate polyline a course without one falls back to is not.

resetSpeed.description: METRES PER SECOND the ship is given along the course at the reset, so it comes back flying rather than hanging. Low: the crash costs you the speed chain and the run-up.

holdSeconds.description: Seconds the sim holds the crashed ship where it hit before the reset. The death curtain (DEV-107) covers this hold; the whole beat is `killSeconds` + this + the cut fade, about a second.

resetClearStepMetres.description: DEV-185. METRES of arc length per step while walking further BACK along the line looking for a reset that is not inside a tree. `clearanceMetres` lifts over the TERRAIN and knows nothing about the forest, and 10 m of `int_01`'s arc resets the ship inside palm #840 — at `resetSpeed`, which is under `breakSpeed`, so it cannot push the tree over and the tree pushes it sideways off the line. The walk is bounded by `resetBackMetres`, so a crash never costs more than twice the ground it already costs; if nothing inside that is clear the shallowest candidate is kept, which is never worse than 0 would have given. 0 switches the whole rule off and is the behaviour that shipped before DEV-185.

crash.description: Arcade crash and reset. DEV-126 (Matt, 2026-09-16: 'we should have player ships crash if they collide too hard - they get reset near their crash spot, but back on the course'). 2016 never crashed: `Ship_HoverShip.OnCollisionEnter` triples angular drag for 0.3 s and plays explode2, `endOnCollide` is 0 on the shipped prefab. The same rule applies to the AI racers, without the curtain.

breakSpeed.description: METRES PER SECOND at or above which a hull contact BREAKS the prop: its collider is removed, a propHit event fires, the renderer swaps the instance for its fractured pieces. Below it the hull bounces off and the prop stands.

breakSlowdown.description: Fraction of the ship's speed a break costs. A tree costs you something and then it is gone.

bounceRestitution.description: How much of the velocity INTO a standing prop comes back out. 0 is the ground's rule (Unity's default material: bounciness 0); a little more than 0 reads as a glance off a trunk rather than a wall.

radiusFraction.description: Collider radius as a fraction of the prop's DRAWN width - the glTF bounds through the same instance matrix the renderer composes, times the placement scale. 0.3 on a tree is the crown, not the trunk: flying through the canopy is a hit.

cellMetres.description: Spatial hash cell, metres. About the widest collider is right; a tick tests the hull's five spheres against nine cells.

fractureSeconds.description: Seconds the paper-cut pieces fly apart along their face normals under (0, -32, 0) and fade before they are removed. Render side only; the sim has forgotten the prop the tick it broke.

racerStuckSeconds.description: DEV-180. SECONDS of unbroken contact after which an AI RACER breaks whatever it is resting on, whatever its speed. 0 switches the escape off. The player never takes this branch: below breakSpeed a player's drift into a trunk is meant to glance, and a player can let go of the stick. A racer cannot - a finished one throttles back to minThrottle (31.4 m/s on fast and cutter, 44.9 on steady and cruiser, against breakSpeed 45) and a crash-reset one arrives at crash.resetSpeed 40 with a cold engine, so for the rest of the run the break branch is closed to it and a palm is a wall it bounces off for ever. 0.25 sits inside a very wide gap rather than at a balance point: a racer that CAN break what it touches is in contact for exactly one tick, and a racer that cannot grinds on for 46-51 consecutive ticks (0.56-0.62 s, measured over four tunings and four approach speeds) while it is scrubbed from 31 m/s to 0.8. There is nothing in between.

strike.description: DEV-428. Matt, 2026-09-26: a struck prop should 'stay standing'. True: a contact at or above breakSpeed costs breakSlowdown and the hitter goes THROUGH, but the collider is KEPT (sim/props/collision.ts `passing`) and the renderer leaves the tree drawn, throwing fx.propBurst instead of DEV-136's fracture. Plants only: a spire (a landmark rock with its own hull) is still removed and fractured, because flying through a standing one would put the eye inside stone. False is DEV-136.

propCollision.description: The props are solid, and they break (DEV-136). Matt, 2026-09-16: 'there are no collision with props - it'd be nice if they broke apart'. 2016 had neither: Tree_Organic_* carries a capsule on a `collider` child, but nothing on the ship reacted to the clones and you flew through the forest. In THIS block and not under `props`, because a contact moves the ship: a Classic run and an Anniversary run of the same stick diverge at the first tree. The AI racers test the same colliders with their own state (DEV-147), and racerStuckSeconds is what gets one off a prop it cannot break (DEV-180).

lockoutScale.description: DEV-410. A multiplier on `hoverjet.energy.RebootTime` (3 s on the shipped prefab): how long boost stays out after the tank empties. 1 is 2016; 0 means no lockout, and an empty tank then boosts on whatever the recharge pays (recharge / burn of the boost's extra thrust).

reengage.description: DEV-410 follow-up. The fraction of the tank it must hold again, after running dry, before boost lights. A ring's refill clears the wait at once. 0 is no wait (2016).

startFill.description: DEV-630 (Matt, 2026-10-04: 'boost should be empty at the start'). The fraction of the tank a run starts with. 1 is 2016, whose `Awake()` fills the tank; 0 starts the run dry, so the first boost is earned by a ring or by the recharge reaching `reengage`.

ringRefill.description: DEV-410. The fraction of the tank that a ring the player takes puts back, clamped at full. 0 is 2016, where a ring pays the boost tank nothing.

rechargeScale.description: Multiplier on `hoverjet.energy.rechargeRate` (100/s on the shipped prefab). The ONE number this block carries; the tank (100), the burn (`engineBurnrate` 8 x `BoostBurnrate` 4 = 32/s) and the empty penalty (`RebootTime` 3 s) all come off the generated sheet. 1 is 2016 exactly - recharge beats burn by +68/s, so the tank never moves and boost is free (DEV-002). At or above burn/recharge = 0.32 nothing can ever empty. 0.16 is a recharge of HALF the burn: 6.25 s of boost from a full tank, a 6.25 s refill, and a 50 % sustainable duty cycle - one design sentence, `you may boost half the lap`. THE NUMBER TO ARGUE WITH, and it is settled by flying it.

energy.description: Boost COSTS energy (DEV-143). Matt, 2026-09-16: 'hold gas + boost as much as you can' feels one-dimensional - and it was in 2016 too, where `EnergySystem_Ship` recharges at 100/s against a 32/s boost burn and recharges WHILE boosting, so the whole reboot subsystem below zero is unreachable. The system was already extracted onto the constants sheet at trust `verified` and nothing in src/ read a key of it. Off, there is no tank at all and boost is the shipped free doubling of thrust; on, it is a resource to spend on the straight and bank through the turn. Empty means NO BOOST for `RebootTime`, never a fall - the fall is the energy race mode.

drainScale.description: Multiplier on `hoverjet.energy.engineBurnrate` (8/s) for the CRUISE drain. Boosting costs x (1 + BoostBurnrate) = 5x that, because `Energy_System.cs` fires BOTH burn branches on a boosting tick - boost is a surcharge on the engine burn, not a replacement for it. 0.2 is 1 / (1 + BoostBurnrate), which makes BOOSTING cost exactly the shipped engineBurnrate of 8/s - a 12.5 s tank - while cruising costs a fifth of it. Sized against a MEASURED 9.9 s from release to the first gate on int_01, the longest gateless stretch either 2016 ghost makes and the stretch that does all the killing at a harsher drain. A zero is refused: a tank that never empties is Ring Attack wearing a gauge.

gatePayFraction.description: What a gate pays, as a fraction of the tank. 0.35 is 35 units, a third of a tank - 4.4 s of boost or 21.9 s of cruise. Swept against both ghosts: cruise and half-boost are comfortable for both, at three-quarters the fast line has 26 units left and the slow line 9, and flat out the fast line finishes on empty while the slow line dies at gate 2. Deliberately NOT `scoring.energyBoostAmount` (12), which is a code-default private constant identical on every gate of every shipped mission and would make a gate worth five seconds. A zero is refused: nothing would refill the tank and every run would end in the sea at the same moment.

energyRace.description: The energy race (DEV-144), the early-prototype mode from the playthrough triage: gates give energy, run dry and you fall. A MODE and not a tweak - `game/modes.ts` gains a fourth row that is Ring Attack in every field but one, and `sim/energy-race.ts` is the tank. The structure is `Energy_System.cs`'s (the PROTOTYPE class, on no shipped prefab, so its initialisers are hypotheses and none is used); every number is `EnergySystem_Ship`'s off the shipped prefab. `enabled` false does not switch a running mode off - it stops the mode being selectable at all, which on Classic it is twice over, since no shipped level chooses it and the generated level schema cannot name it.

maxCount.description: Ceiling on the LEVEL's own `count`, for this edition - the frame budget, and the one number a headset pass turns. Separate from `AMBIENT_TRAFFIC_MAX` in src/content/level-schema.ts, which is a structural cap on authored content: that one says 'nobody meant this number', this one says 'this many ships fit in the frame'.

recycleClearMetres.description: Metres from the player inside which a ship that has finished its lap is NOT put back to the start of its line. A recycle is a teleport; deferring it until the ship is far away makes it IMPOSSIBLE to see rather than unlikely to be seen (DEV-041's distinction). A finished ship keeps flying out, climbing away, until it is past this.

ambientTraffic.description: DEV-146. Matt, 2026-09-16: 'Interleaved modes: see HoverJets fly while on a JumpSeat course.' WHICH course the traffic flies is the LEVEL's (`ambientTraffic` in content/levels/*.json, emitted by tools/extract/level.mjs from an authored table) because it differs per island; this is the switch and the frame budget. In the GAMEPLAY block though it scores nothing, because it puts bodies in the world on the same fixed tick - the score is identical between editions, the work is not. 2016 had nothing of the kind, so Classic is off.

variants.description: DEV-380, docs/plan/AIRCRAFT-VARIANTS.md section 8. Matt, 2026-09-24: 'a new selection after the aircraft type.' Whether the variant step EXISTS, and nothing else: the variants are properties of the aircraft, not of a look preset, so they live in content/aircraft/<vehicle>.json and this block carries no numbers. In the GAMEPLAY block because a variant changes the machine - the same stick on a speed variant is a different run. Off, it is 2016 exactly: resolveVariant returns standard whatever is stored or in ?variant=, so the flight is built from the sheet itself.

glider.description: DEV-399, docs/plan/AIRCRAFT-VARIANTS.md section 5 (G1). Whether the GLIDER is an aircraft in this edition, and nothing else: its numbers are its own file's, content/aircraft/glider.json. On, its courses join the level list (the fleet levelIds() filters by) and the hangar has a third aircraft table. Off is 2016 exactly: 2016 authored a glider and shipped it switched off at every level (DEV-145), so a Classic hangar has two aircraft and never lists a glider course.

rooms.description: DEV-389, plan/MULTIPLAYER.md section 6.3. Whether this preset races in ROOMS (live multiplayer). Its people stand on the racers' own starts, one each (DEV-477): the player's pad, then gameplay.racers' list, as src/game/racer-grid.ts roomStarts lays it out. Left out of every lap's rules string (src/net/lap-courses-build.ts): a room lap never goes on a solo board. A PREVIEW_ONLY block (src/content/build-channel.ts).

editor.description: DEV-466, docs/plan/EDITOR.md section 5.7. Whether the COURSE EDITOR and player courses (links, .ffcourse files, Your courses) are offered, and nothing else. A PREVIEW_ONLY block (src/content/build-channel.ts): a release build turns it off. Left out of every lap's rules string (src/net/lap-courses-build.ts RULES_IGNORE): it decides what the menus offer, not what a lap is. The menus wear Anniversary (D35), so they read Anniversary's block.

headsetCuts.description: DEV-481 follow-up. In a headset, TV's comfort cuts (trackside vantages through black, teleport and snap turn) instead of the flat camera. False at launch (Matt, 2026-10-01: keep it functionally identical to flat). Inside tv, so outside every lap's rules.

tv.description: DEV-480, docs/plan/FF-TV.md section 5.1. Whether FACETED FLIGHT TV is offered (the title's TV row, the ?tv links, the results panel's watch link), and nothing else. A PREVIEW_ONLY block (src/content/build-channel.ts): a release build turns it off until Matt has worn it, and taking it off that list is the 1.0 shipping edit. Left out of every lap's rules string (src/net/lap-courses-build.ts RULES_IGNORE): it decides what the menus offer, not what a lap is. The menus wear Anniversary (D35), so they read Anniversary's block.

scale.description: Per-KIND multipliers on 2016's own scatter scales (DEV-134). Keyed by the palette entry's `kind` as tools/extract/props.mjs classified its pack; a kind that is absent multiplies by 1. Measured through the renderer's own instance matrix against the glTF bounds: alpine's shipped Tree_Organic pass stands 15-83 m tall and its never-run Tree Pack pass 11-78 m, against 20-45 m for a mature conifer (the 2016 video, 0:55, shows the pad's nearest trees at about the 35 m gate's height); desert's cacti 15-46 m against a saguaro's 12-15; the palms 18-37 m; the bushes 1.6-4.8 m. EMPTY on Classic: it multiplies nothing and draws 2016's sizes. The count does not change with the size, so a smaller tree is a sparser forest - the density is 2016's and stays.

sink.description: METRES a prop's base is buried below the rendered facet it stands on. On top of the mesh's own base offset (the Tree Pack trunks start 0.03-0.11 m below their origin, times the scale). A trunk on a slope shows air on its downhill side by radius x tan(slope); this hides it for the trunks the forest has.

groundSnap.description: Put every 2016-scattered prop on the RENDERED surface rather than on the source height map (DEV-134). 2016's GenerateObjects() reads SourceHeightMap and subtracts ObjectHeightOffset; the mesh you see is that map plus RandomOffset (0.8 m on alpine) of jitter per vertex, so a trunk stands on a point the facet under it moved away from. And the alpine pass only Anniversary draws (DEV-102) carries heightOffset -2.6, which RAISES every one of its trees 2.6 m: they hung 0.4-2.4 m in the air before the jitter. Off on Classic, which keeps 2016's rule - including the shipped pass's heightOffset 5, which buries its trees five metres and never floats.

scatterShadows.description: Whether the SCATTER draws into the shadow map as well as into the frame (DEV-224). True is 2016's caster set; false takes the scatter out of the caster set and NOTHING else out - the land at LOD 0, the hand-placed landmarks and the ship's exterior hull all keep casting, and the scatter keeps RECEIVING, so a tree still darkens under the ridge behind it. Since DEV-304 (wishlist #33) it is TRUE on Anniversary and listed in `vr.disable`, which is §0's "on in flat, off in VR" rather than a change of mind about DEV-224's number: switching the whole depth pass off measured 2.70 ms p50 on adv_01_hoverJet through a real SteamVR compositor with a 0.01 ms bracket (docs/plan/VR-PERF-WAVE-3.md section 5), against a flat build that has 1.02 ms of GPU and nothing to buy. The scatter is 88-93 % of desert's and alpine's world pass (7.42 M triangles in 18 draw calls on desert, identical across all four of its missions) and the shadow pass draws every one of them a second time, which is what that 2.70 ms is. Inert on Classic, where render.shadows.enabled is false and no object is given a flag at all. Off at quality `low` whatever this says, because the map itself is. IT IS COUPLED TO render.canopyShade AND THE COUPLING IS IN CODE, not in a clause: DEV-295's bake may darken the DIRECT sun only while nothing else is darkening the same ground, so `render/shadows.ts`'s `canopyDirectWeight` hands the direct half over to the map whenever this flag really resolves true - preset, quality tier and `vr.disable` composed - and `render/far-shadow.ts` applies it as a uniform, live, with no recompile. DEV-304.

from.description: METRES from the camera to a chunk's NEAREST point at which this rung takes over. Strictly ascending across the list.

keep.description: Fraction of the mesh's distinct corners this rung keeps. Strictly descending across the list. The triangle count falls roughly with it: on desert's 1,520-triangle bush, 0.25 keeps 346 and 0.1 keeps 130.

rungs.description: The coarser rungs, nearest first. Rung 0, the full mesh, is implicit.

meshLod.description: Coarser meshes for the far scatter (DEV-338). Each rung is a copy of every scatter mesh simplified at LOAD to `keep` of its distinct corners -- three's SimplifyModifier on the welded positions, then each surviving face painted the colour of the nearest source face, so a rung is still one colour per face (ART_DIRECTION pillar 2) and still every colour is one the artist chose. A chunk draws rung k once its NEAREST point is `from` metres from the camera (horizontal, like 2016's own scan), with the pass's FlipFlopPercent as hysteresis at every edge; the chunk's centre and 2016's LODDistance still decide the outer edge, untouched. Changing rung is 2016's staggered reveal run between two meshes: over lodTransitionTime a shuffled ceil(total * percent) of the chunk leaves the old rung for the new, so nothing changes as a block and no prop is ever on both or neither. `rungs` is read at WORLD BUILD, because it decides which meshes exist; `enabled` is read at every 1/30 s scan, so a live flip walks the forest back to rung 0 by the same staggered swap. Empty rungs build nothing, which is Classic.

sin.description: SINE of the steepest rendered facet a scatter prop may stand on: 0 is flat, 0.5 is 30 degrees, 0.7 is 44, 1 is a wall. The unit the dressing's slopeMin/slopeMax are written in, so one number means one thing across this file.

maxSlope.description: No 2016-scatter prop on steep ground (DEV-356). Matt: "don't place props on steep slopes." A placement whose RENDERED facet -- the triangle of the jittered 8 m vertex grid the terrain draws, the one groundSnap stands the trunk on (sim/terrain/surface.ts) -- is steeper than `sin` is dropped at LOAD, beside the no-prop volumes and before the snap, the chunk layout and the colliders, so it is neither drawn nor solid. A SUBTRACTION: every surviving placement keeps its position, yaw, palette and scale bit-for-bit, and the baked blob is untouched (hard rule 3). 2016's GenerateObjects() had no slope term at all -- one roll per density texel -- and its own baked clones stand on steep ground as often as the port's re-roll does, so this is a deviation and Classic is false. The DRESSING (props.scatter's bands) is not filtered by it: its bands carry their own slopeMin/slopeMax, and the boulders are there for the cliffs. Read at world build, like groundSnap. `?feature=props.maxSlope:off` is the A/B.

seed.description: The placement PRNG's seed. Not a 2016 concept — 2016's scatter ran once in the editor on an unseeded `UnityEngine.Random` and baked its answer (PROP-AUDIT section 4). Ours is seeded for the same reason the terrain generator is: same seed, same world, forever, and a layout somebody likes can be kept by writing a number down.

clearance.description: METRES of clear air kept around the racing LINE and around every gate centre. Measured in three dimensions to the line, not to the nearest control point — DEV-027 is the whole reason that sentence is worth writing, because nearest-vertex said 24.6 m where the line says 0.4. Three dimensions and not two, so a boulder on the ground under a route point 300 m up is not in the way and is not thrown away.

variants.description: How many seeded mesh variants each KIND is generated in. Capped at 4 because the renderer packs every variant of a kind into one geometry and swaps between them per instance — one draw call per kind, at the cost of one vertex attribute per extra variant.

kind.description: Which generated mesh family. Two bands of the same kind cost ONE draw call, not two — which is why a steep band and a shoreline band can both be boulders.

density.description: Instances per SQUARE KILOMETRE of terrain, before the slope, altitude and clearance bands reject any. An island is 4096 m square, so 16.8 km2; a density of 300 is about 5,000 candidates of which the bands keep whatever fits. It is a candidate rate and not a promise, and `dressing.test.ts` prints what it actually produced.

scaleMin.description: METRES ACROSS, at the small end. The generated mesh is normalised to exactly 1 m wide, so this multiplies directly and the number means the thing it says — which is the entire point of the class (ANNIVERSARY.md section 1.1: familiar size works at any distance, and only if the size is familiar).

scaleMax.description: Metres across, at the large end. Must not be below `scaleMin`.

slopeMin.description: SIN of the ground's angle: 0 is flat, 0.5 is 30 degrees, 0.87 is 60, 1 is a cliff. Boulders belong on steep ground and at cliff feet; shrubs on gentle ground. `sin` rather than the gradient so the number is bounded and readable.

slopeMax.description: The top of the slope band.

altitudeMin.description: METRES. World y when `nearWater` is false — Simonet's sea is at about 116 m and its peaks reach 1,000 — or metres above the LOCAL water surface when it is true.

altitudeMax.description: The top of the altitude band, same units as `altitudeMin`.

nearWater.description: Measure the altitude band from the water rather than from world zero. One flag with one meaning, and it is how a shoreline band gets written without a second pair of keys. An environment with no ocean — the desert canyon — places nothing from a `nearWater` band at all, which is right.

tint.description: How far the instance's colour is pulled toward the GROUND's own colour, sampled off the environment's colour map at the placement. 0 is the palette alone; 1 is the hillside's colour exactly. It is what makes a boulder on red rock red-brown and one on the green ridge grey-green, from one palette and one draw call.

environments.description: Environment ids this band applies to (`simonet`, `kauai`, `desert`, `alpine`). Absent or empty means all of them. This is how kauai and the desert differ without a partial-override merge: two bands, two densities, two lists.

scatter.description: The classes of familiar-size object and the ground each belongs on. ANNIVERSARY.md section 1.5 item 6, section 3.2 V9, DEV-089. EMPTY on Classic, which draws exactly the 1,241 palms it drew before.

unbakedPasses.description: Draw 2016's generator passes that 2016 never RAN (DEV-102; Matt, 2026-09-14: keep them for Anniversary). `FacetedTerrain`'s scatter is an editor-time `GenerateObjects()` whose output is serialised on the component, and three of the port's five passes serialised ZERO objects — alpine's big-tree pass, and the palm generators on Simonet and Kauai. Classic draws what 2016 SHIPPED; Anniversary draws what 2016 SET UP. The predicate is `bakedObjects > 0` off each environment JSON's own `shipped2016` block — the COUNT, not the component's enabled flag, because that is DEV-102's whole lesson. A flag only: there is nothing to tune, the passes are 2016's own parameters. Read at world build, so a live EDITION flip does not restack the trees under you.

flocks.description: How many flocks are placed along the course, spread evenly by ARC LENGTH so they are met one at a time. Fewer are placed than asked for if a course cannot fit one clear of the line.

birdsPerFlock.description: Birds in each. All flocks together are ONE draw call.

altitude.description: METRES above the ground under the loop's centre — not above sea level, and not above the route. A flock circling 55 m over a ridge is a scale cue for the ridge.

radius.description: Metres: the loop's mean radius. The ellipse's two axes are drawn around it.

speed.description: METRES PER SECOND at the flock's mean radius. Half the flocks fly the loop the other way.

size.description: METRES, wing tip to wing tip, varied a little per bird. A gull is about one, and that is the whole cue: a metre at 100 m is a known angle, so the ridge behind it gets a ruler laid on it (ANNIVERSARY.md section 2.5 S5 — a flock is a scale cue AND a speed cue).

birds.description: Flocks near the course: seeded ellipses, tilted a little, at an altitude over the ground they circle, with the wings beating in the vertex shader out of step. Ambience on the RENDER clock, never the sim. ANNIVERSARY.md section 2.5 S5, DEV-089.

props.description: More classes of familiar-size object — boulders, rocks, shrubs and birds — generated, seeded and scattered by RULE rather than by 2016's density maps, which are the palms'. The diagnosis is ANNIVERSARY.md section 1.4: with nothing human-sized on the ground the eye assumes the facets are ordinary clutter, and a 35 m gate reads as a 4 m one. DEV-089.

speedUnit.description: What the SPEED row is measured in. `ms` is what shipped: `HudState.speed` is metres per second and the panel prints the rounded number with no unit, so 170 is 612 km/h and nothing says so. `kmh` converts for display and appends the unit to the VALUE column; the LABEL still comes from `level.ui` and is untouched. Not a feature flag — there is no 'off' — so it does not appear in `editionFeatures`, and Classic's value is `ms` rather than false. ANNIVERSARY.md S8.

coneDegrees.description: DEGREES off the nose inside which the arrow HIDES. The target is in front of you; the arrow has nothing to add. THE NUMBER TO ARGUE WITH: too small and it nags on every straight, too big and it is silent through the turn it exists for.

featherDegrees.description: DEGREES beyond the cone over which the arrow grows from nothing to full length, so a target drifting across the cone edge does not blink it.

lengthMetres.description: METRES, base to tip. It sits about 0.8 m from the eye, so 0.08 m subtends about 5.7 degrees — big enough to read in peripheral vision, small enough not to cover the gate it points at.

offset.description: METRES from the EYE in the SHIP's frame — three space, so forward is -z and up is +y. Where on the glareshield the arrow sits. It is parented to the ship like the HUD (`render/hud.ts` says why a head-locked instrument is the wrong choice) and moves neither the rig nor the cockpit mesh (ART_DIRECTION pillar 3).

color.description: Linear RGB of the arrow. An instrument, so it is allowed the dash-lamp register (DEV-088) rather than the world's.

emissive.description: Emissive intensity. The arrow is read in shadow as often as in sun, so it carries its own light like the dash does.

nextGateArrow.description: A paper-cut arrow on the glareshield pointing at the next gate — the next ring, then the finish; the nearest open pad on a JumpSeat course; nothing in Free Flight. Hidden while the target is inside the forward cone. Matt, 2026-09-16: *"i could use a 'next gate' indicator arrow towards the front of the cockpit to help me understand where to fly."* DEV-124.

widthMetres.description: METRES across the plate. Its height is the readout panel's own (0.145 m), so the two plates line up. THE NUMBER TO ARGUE WITH: the course is fitted to it uniformly, so a wider plate is a bigger map on a wide course and only more margin on a tall one.

gapMetres.description: METRES between the panel's right edge and the plate's left edge. The smaller it is, the less of a glance the map costs from the panel. 0.03 is the perf plate's own `PLATE_GAP` on the other side, and at the flat seat's ~660 px per metre it keeps the map out of the 12-18 px margins the HUD pixel specs crop around the panel.

dotMetres.description: METRES corner to corner of a racer's hexagon. The course line's stroke is a fixed share of it, so the two scale together.

playerDotMetres.description: METRES corner to corner of a hexagon, before its ring. The player's mark was that hexagon until DEV-432; it is now a triangle pointing along the nose with the SAME AREA, so this still sets how much of the plate the mark covers. Bigger than a racer's AND ringed: king-tide's playtest found a same-size dot could not be told from the field.

raceMap.description: The course from above with a dot per ship, and the player's place (`P2/6`), on a plate beside the readout — a child of it, so it follows the placement, the third-person camera and the pause menu. Only where the mode's rules have opponents and live AI racers fly. Geometry, not a canvas: one draw call, no texture, no raster (HUD-REWORK). Matt, 2026-09-24: *"simplified race mini map hud to understand your position relative to others - grab from king-tide"*. DEV-361.

bars.description: The panel's two bars: the gate combo's countdown under GATES and the boost tank under TIME (DEV-615). 2016's panel drew no bars, so Classic turns them off; the JumpSeat's fuel gauge is 2016's own instrument and is not this flag's. Matt, 2026-10-07: go with the recommendation (QUESTIONS item 7). DEV-791.

hud.description: The cockpit readout. Presentation only: the panel is a pure consumer of `HudState` and every value on it comes from the run, not from the preset.

vr.description: Features this preset turns OFF while a headset is presenting (and, since DEV-934, a short list of named VR VALUES in `override`), so the VR look is a SUBSET of the flat one but for those values. DEV-263, Matt 2026-09-21: “off in VR, on in flat.” Optional: absent means the preset is the same in both places, which is what Classic is. A deliberately narrow shape: a deep-partial preset would let VR change any number, which is two looks to art-direct and every future field silently acquiring a second value nobody set.

disable.description: Paths from `editionFeatures()` in src/content/edition-schema.ts, each forced to `enabled: false` while presenting. The loader refuses a path that is not in that registry, so a typo cannot quietly disable nothing — which matters because the only symptom of that would be a frame rate. NO `uniqueItems` here on purpose: this repo's validator (tests/unit/helpers/json-schema.ts) refuses keywords it does not implement rather than ignoring them, and `validateEdition` already rejects a repeated path with a message that names the file. One check, in the place that runs at load.

perEntry.description: Why each entry is on the list, keyed by the same path. Prose only; nothing reads it.

override.description: DEV-934: VR-only VALUES, keyed by `editionFeatures()` path, each an object of that feature's own fields set while presenting (plus an optional `note`, prose). validateEdition refuses a path that is not a feature or is a RULES key (edition-split.ts), a path vr.disable turns off, `enabled` (on and off are disable's), a field the feature does not have, and a value not the flat value's exact shape. So nothing can be added or turned on in VR and no rule can differ; what moves is a number somebody wrote down here by name. `props.meshLod.rungs` may move each `from` and never a `keep` (DEV-935: the meshes are made once, at world build).

boundary.description: The out-of-bounds warning, drawn. 2016 shows a HUD panel and logs a line a second (PlayerBoundary.cs, HUD_Ship.ShowOutOfBounds) — no screen effect — so Classic has none of this. DEV-127.

fuzz.description: Signal-loss static over the frame while the 13 s countdown runs, growing with it. It comes in from the corners and closes on the centre with the clock, so the middle of the frame — and the RETURN banner — stay readable until the final second. Not scaled by the speed-FX comfort slider: it is feedback, not vection (src/render/boundary-fuzz.ts).

strength.description: OVERLAY ALPHA of the static at the outermost pixel at the moment the clock reaches zero. The live level is this times the countdown progress. 1 is total signal loss. THE NUMBER TO ARGUE WITH.

waitForExit.description: Start the clock when the ship LEAVES the gate's trigger sphere rather than when it enters it (DEV-195). 2016 counts from OnTriggerEnter, and on a 22.619 m trigger sphere that fires a measured median of 21.5 m BEFORE the gate's own plane — over 129 crossings, a 0.3 s shrink anchored there leaves the gate at 0.675 of its size (0.390 at the 5th percentile) by the time the ship reaches the plane. Capped at `props.checkpointRing.passedHideDelay` so a gate can never fail to go away. False is 2016's anchor and is what Classic runs whatever this says.

delaySeconds.description: SIM seconds after the ANCHOR (the pass, or the exit under waitForExit) before the gate starts to go. 2016 held for 2 s (`props.checkpointRing.passedHideDelay`, a coroutine literal in TriggerCheckpoint.Deactivate()), which is what Classic runs whatever this says.

seconds.description: SIM seconds the shrink takes once it starts. 0 is a pop — 2016's behaviour, and what the flag exists to replace. THE NUMBER TO ARGUE WITH.

passedFade.description: How a PASSED gate leaves (DEV-122). 2016: two seconds, then gone in one frame — `checkpointArt.SetActive(false)` on the `offset` node both the frame and the stud cage hang under, for the PLAYER's pass only (the npc branch hides nothing), in any order. Classic does exactly that. Anniversary replaces the pop with a short shrink about the gate's centre, so the gate you just threaded folds away rather than blinking out — anchored on the EXIT rather than the entry since DEV-195, because a pass is stamped on the trigger sphere's IN edge and that is 22 m before the gate.

columns.description: Cells across. WHOLE, 2 or more, so the chequer alternates.

cellMetres.description: METRES per cell pitch in the world. Absolute rather than a fraction of the frame, because what the eye reads at 500 m is a size, not a ratio.

gap.description: 0-1: fraction of each pitch left EMPTY. This is what notches the silhouette; 0 is a solid band.

lift.description: METRES between the frame's top edge and the bottom of the band.

light.description: Linear RGB of the light cells.

dark.description: Linear RGB of the dark cells.

emissive.description: Emissive intensity on the LIGHT cells. Gate frames already glow (ART_DIRECTION, what may glow), so this is the same allowance, not a new one.

finishBanner.description: A chequered, crenellated band on the FINISH gate's top edge (DEV-123). 2016 marks the finish by colour and size alone — the ring's own frame, orange, at three times a ring's scale — and ART_DIRECTION pillar 1's black cut-out of that is a nearer ring. This gives it a silhouette: separated cells notch the outline, and a chequered flag is the one finish sign nobody is taught. Classic draws 2016's finish untouched.

gates.description: The course's gates as objects in the world: how a passed one leaves, and how the finish is told from the rest. Render only, never the sim — the trigger volumes are untouched by anything here.

life.description: The life pass: scenery that moves (DEV-447 boats; DEV-449 dolphins, its own row; DEV-545 cut DEV-449's fish, Matt 2026-09-30: “kill the fish”; DEV-448's spectators were cut by DEV-463). Matt, 2026-09-27: “would like the "life" pass to come online sometime soon.” A TOP-LEVEL block and not a key in `gameplay`: nothing here can change a lap, and a `gameplay` key restarts the Anniversary boards. 2016 had none of it, so Classic's every flag is off. Life is never an opponent, never a collider and never a score (DEV-146's rule, `game/ambient-traffic.ts`).

boats.description: Moored and anchored boats on the sea, near the shore and near the start (DEV-447). Placed by RULE over the course's own line and spawn (`sim/life/boats.ts`), so a new mission gets boats without touching `src/` and an environment with no sea gets none. Each boat rides the triangle the sea is DRAWN with (`sim/life/sea-facet.ts` rebuilds it bit for bit; the wave is `render/water.ts`'s own), so it heaves and rolls with the facet under it rather than floating on a surface nobody can see. One instanced mesh, one draw call, per kind. The meshes are 2016's own bought Geometric-Landscape pack (`GL-Manmade-08`, `-13`), which 2016 bought and never placed.

minQuality.description: The lowest comfort quality that still draws the boats. Below it the fleet is hidden (no draw calls); the build and the placement are kept, so a quality change back shows them again at once.

seed.description: Folded with the course id (FNV-1a), so each course has its own harbour and the same course has the same one on every load.

alongRoute.description: Boats aimed at evenly spaced fractions of the course's line, `(i + 0.5) / n` — the traffic's own half-open spacing (DEV-146). A course with no line has only the start boats.

atStart.description: Boats aimed at the spawn, where the launch breaches the sea and the player is at the water's height, slowly.

routeReach.description: METRES out from each line point that are searched, `[min, max]`, in rings.

startReach.description: METRES out from the spawn that are searched, `[min, max]`. The min keeps a mast out of the launch deck's footprint (DEV-100's 52 m clearing) and the launch path.

depth.description: METRES of water under the hull, `[min, max]`: the sea's base height minus the island's. Shallow enough to be near a shore, deep enough not to be aground. Off the island's map is open ocean and fails any finite band. THE NUMBERS TO ARGUE WITH for how close to the beach the boats sit.

startOpenWater.description: The START boats keep `depth`'s floor and drop its ceiling, so they may anchor in deep or open sea. They are there to watch a race start, and on `int_01_hoverJet` the start deck stands in open sea beyond the island's map, where there is no shore to moor to.

spacing.description: METRES between any two boats, centre to centre.

swing.description: DEGREES either side of the fleet's one shared heading. Moored boats swing to one wind; a bay of boats pointing every way reads as dropped rather than moored.

step.description: METRES between search rings, and between samples along each ring (its arc), so a narrow shelf far out is not stepped over.

angles.description: The fewest directions tried on a ring, from a seeded start; a wide ring gets more (one every `step` of arc).

mesh.description: The converted GLB under the asset base, `assets/life/…` (tools/assets/convert-life.mjs).

weight.description: Relative share of the fleet. 0 leaves the kind out.

scale.description: Uniform scale on the mesh as converted, `[min, max]`. The Geometric-Landscape pack is modelled at about half size (a 1.2 m parasol, a 0.4 m fence), and 2016 already drew its palms at 4-8x.

draft.description: MESH METRES of hull under the water (the keel is the mesh's y = 0), before `scale`.
